recreation_center: Cohon University Center fitness center (10,000 sq ft, two stories) + Wiegand Gym + pools [CMU-S43]
best_fit_reason: A purpose-built AI degree with a real statistics spine (36-401), four mandatory AI clusters reaching graduate-level courses, research courses inside the major, first-year-eligible funded research, and a no-GPA-gate honors thesis [CMU-S1][CMU-S14][CMU-S13]. evidence_confidence: medium-high — curriculum, admission structure, research programs, cost, housing, and recreation are all officially verified; course-schedule frequency and major-specific outcomes are not

score_notes.math_foundations: Seven math/stats courses including 21-241 linear algebra, 21-259 multivariable, and 36-401 Modern Regression [CMU-S1].
score_notes.ai_curriculum_breadth: Four mandatory AI clusters span robotics/decision-making, ML, perception & language, and human-AI interaction [CMU-S1].
score_notes.ai_curriculum_depth: Cluster electives are graduate-cross-listed (10-403 Deep RL, 10-417 Deep Learning, 16-350 Planning for Robotics) [CMU-S1].
score_notes.emerging_ai_topics: 10-423 Generative AI is an approved cluster elective and an ethics course is required, but no named AI-agents course was verified [CMU-S1].
score_notes.curricular_flexibility: ~360 units with 7 humanities, 4 science/engineering, and a required cognitive-science course leaves a modest free-elective margin [CMU-S1][CMU-S3].
score_notes.course_availability: The SCS schedule page I reached still served Fall 2025 data, so cluster-elective offering frequency could not be confirmed [CMU-S78].
score_notes.undergraduate_research_access: SURF is open to first-years at $4,500 for 8–10 weeks, and the SCS honors thesis (07-599) has no GPA requirement [CMU-S14][CMU-S13].
score_notes.faculty_mentorship: 07-300/07-400 research courses sit inside the major and faculty run public 07-280/07-380 course sites, but no central lab-matching program was found [CMU-S8][CMU-S9].
score_notes.project_based_learning: Research practicum courses plus a student-run 24/7 machine shop and TechSpark fabrication access [CMU-S8][CMU-S51][CMU-S56].
score_notes.robotics_autonomy_options: Bachelor of Science in Robotics (BSR) (no ABET); 15 undergrad robotics courses. 40 labs, RI, 3 competition teams.
score_notes.computing_resources: No undergraduate-facing GPU or cluster allocation page was verified this session.
score_notes.industry_preparation: The most recent official SCS figure is 98% employed or in grad school with $125,845 average starting salary, but it is dated January 2022 [CMU-S64].
score_notes.graduate_school_preparation: Honors thesis with no GPA gate plus RISS (~80% of scholars continue research remotely) support PhD preparation; external placement data not published [CMU-S13][CMU-S21].
score_notes.fourplusone_quality: BSAI graduates are eligible for the 5th-Year MS but must complete extra CS breadth first, and no scholarships or financial assistance are offered [CMU-S25][CMU-S26].
score_notes.intellectual_energy: ~40 student-taught StuCo courses run per term and TartanHacks 2026 was billed as Pittsburgh's largest hackathon [CMU-S23][CMU-S59].
score_notes.healthy_ambition: Students report most CMU classes are not curved and little interpersonal competition, but official/journalistic sources document stress rising to 58% high-risk by finals week [CMU-S67][CMU-S74].
score_notes.student_agency: Undergraduates teach for-credit 98-xxx courses and run a 24/7 machine shop for ~$30/year in dues [CMU-S23][CMU-S51].
score_notes.community_within_scale: SCS has 999 undergraduates inside a 7,824-undergraduate university, and 65% of students live on campus all four years [CMU-S60][CMU-S61][CMU-S38].
score_notes.technical_club_ecosystem: Roboclub dates to 1984 with a machine shop, 3D printers, and laser cutter; ScottyLabs ran TartanHacks Feb 6–7, 2026 [CMU-S51][CMU-S59].
score_notes.nonacademic_club_variety: StuCo offerings include Private Pilot Ground School alongside technical minis, but the full activities directory was not verified [CMU-S23].
score_notes.non_greek_social_life: Greek life is 19% of the student body (1,100+ members) and does not control housing, since first-years must live on campus and 65% stay four years [CMU-S36][CMU-S38].
score_notes.campus_engagement: Buggy/Sweepstakes has run since 1920 and 2026 Spring Carnival ran April 9–11 with race day April 11 [CMU-S46][CMU-S48].
score_notes.recreation_facilities: Cohon Center offers a 10,000 sq ft, two-story fitness center with 60+ cardio machines, pools, and squash courts, open to all students on CMU ID with 30–35 free weekly Group X classes [CMU-S43][CMU-S41][CMU-S45].
score_notes.daily_life: The $302 transportation fee bundles PRT public-transit access plus campus shuttle in urban Pittsburgh; winter draws repeated student complaints [CMU-S34][CMU-S69].

admissions.admit_rate_note_note: CMU's CDS does not publish an in-state vs out-of-state admit split.
admissions.major_admit_context: CMU admits by college and by program, and the spread is enormous. In CMU's own publication, the School of Computer Science 'now turns away almost 95 percent of those who apply': in the cited year 6,756 students applied to SCS and only 350 were admitted, 'a rate of less than 5.2 percent. ... Compare that to the 19 percent acceptance rate for CMU's other seven undergraduate programs' [CMU-S5]. Testing requirements also differ by college for the most recently published cycle: SCS requires the SAT or ACT, the College of Fine Arts is test-optional, and the College of Engineering, Dietrich, Heinz Information Systems, Mellon College of Science and Tepper are 'test flexible' — applicants must submit some standardized evidence (SAT, ACT, IB, AP, Cambridge A-Level or French Baccalaureate) [CMU-S4]. The College of Engineering admits directly to a department/major unless the applicant selects undecided [CMU-S6]. Early Decision is materially easier: 553 admits from 2,680 ED applicants (20.6%) versus 11.07% overall [CMU-S1]. Robotics at the undergraduate level is a minor rather than a major — the Robotics Institute offers 'masters programs and an undergraduate minor for Carnegie Mellon students' [CMU-S8].
admissions.ea_admit_rate_note: CDS C22 Early Action = No, and CMU states plainly: 'Carnegie Mellon does not offer early action.'
admissions.pct_submitting_sat_note: 1,182 enrolled first-years submitted SAT scores (65.5%); 327 submitted ACT (18.1%).
admissions.gpa_note: CDS C12 average high school GPA 3.89, reported for 99.7% of enrolled first-years; CDS C10 shows 82.5% in the top tenth of their high school class.
admissions.test_policy_note: Not test-optional. The School of Computer Science requires an SAT or ACT score. The College of Engineering, Dietrich, MCS, Tepper and Heinz are 'test flexible', which CMU defines as scores being REQUIRED with a choice of test type (SAT, ACT, IB, AP, Cambridge A-Level, French Bac). Only the College of Fine Arts is test optional. CDS C7 lists test scores as merely 'Considered', which describes weight, not whether they must be submitted. Testing preferred complete by November 1 for Early Decision.

decision_dates.restrictions: ED is binding and is not available for the School of Drama, BXA Design or the School of Music. Regular Decision for Drama and Music closes December 1. There is no Early Action and no rolling admission, and there is no ED II.

why_us_ammunition: The Robotics Institute 'was established in 1979 to conduct basic and applied research in robotics technologies' and founded 'the world's first Robotics PhD program' in 1989 — the deepest institutional robotics lineage available to cite [CMU-S8].

RI facilities span roughly 100,000 sq ft on the Pittsburgh campus plus another 100,000 sq ft at the National Robotics Engineering Center in Lawrenceville, so an applicant can point to specific research infrastructure [CMU-S8].
Undergraduates engage robotics through an RI undergraduate minor rather than a major — an honest, well-informed applicant should frame robotics as a minor layered on an SCS or CIT major [CMU-S8].
The College of Engineering admits directly to a department, so a Why-Us essay can and should argue for a specific department rather than the university in general [CMU-S6].

CMU's own reporting that SCS 'turns away almost 95 percent' of applicants versus roughly 19 percent for its other undergraduate programs is useful for explaining a considered college choice within CMU [CMU-S5].

door.how_you_enter: You apply to the College of Engineering and are admitted directly to the ECE department/major (or as CoE undecided); the School of Computer Science is an entirely separate admit unit.
door.easier_than_cs_basis: CMU's first-party admission and SCS undergraduate pages publish no current per-college or per-major admit rates (CMU-E2, CMU-E4), so no published comparison of the CoE/ECE door with the SCS door exists. What is documented is that they are separate doors: 'Students applying to the College of Engineering apply to and are admitted directly to a department/major unless choosing undecided' (CMU-E2).
door.internal_gate: Graduation QPA of 2.0 required after freshman year; ECE department courses require a minimum 2.0 QPA and prerequisite courses require a grade of C or better (18-202 specifically C or better) (CMU-E1). Robotics Additional Major requires a 3.0 GPA to apply and a 3.0 QPA in the additional-major curriculum to graduate (CMU-E3).

ece.vs_cs: ECE at CMU is a genuinely different door from SCS: ECE is admitted through the College of Engineering while CS/AI/Robotics majors are admitted through SCS, and ECE's own course set already covers controls (18-370, 18-474), autonomous robotics (18-442), mechatronics (18-578), vision (18-395, 18-794) and ML for engineers (18-461/18-462). Crucially, an ECE student can still reach the Robotics Additional Major, which is 'Open to students across all majors and colleges at Carnegie Mellon University' at a 3.0 GPA, and the Machine Learning Minor, which is explicitly reserved for undergraduates 'outside the School of Computer Science' — so ECE, not CS, is the major that unlocks the ML minor. The cost is a hardware-heavy core (circuits, devices, 18-220/18-240/18-290) and the fact that CMU publishes no admit-rate evidence that the CoE door is actually easier.
ece.notable: Integrated Master's/Bachelor's (IMB) into the Professional M.S. in ECE is guaranteed at 270+ units with a 3.00 QPA, with no separate application and no GRE (CMU-E1). Robotics Additional Major lets non-CS majors double count up to six courses (CS majors only five) (CMU-E3). The Machine Learning Minor is open to any major outside SCS (CMU-E5).

door.how_you_enter: You apply to Cornell Engineering as your college, not to ECE: 'Cornell University only allows applicants to apply to one of the seven undergraduate colleges and schools' and 'No, you do not apply to a particular major; you apply to the college' — you may indicate an intended major, and 'You do not officially select your major until the second semester of your sophomore year' (CORNELL-E2, CORNELL-E3).
door.easier_than_cs_basis: Cornell publishes admissions decisions at the college level, not by major, and no first-party per-major admit rates for ECE or CS were found. The structural point is that you apply to a college rather than a major, and ECE and Engineering-side CS sit in the same college, so the college choice matters more than the major label (CORNELL-E2).
door.internal_gate: ECE affiliation requires at least a C+ in MATH 2930 or 2940, in PHYS 2213, and in one of ECE 2100/ENGRD 2100, ECE 2720 or ECE 2300/ENGRD 2300, plus a GPA of at least 2.5 across the listed math, physics and ECE gateway courses (CORNELL-E1).

ece.vs_cs: The decisive Cornell fact is that you apply to one of seven colleges and not to a major: Cornell Engineering is the single wrapper for both ECE and Engineering-side CS, so ECE is not a lower-selectivity backdoor but a different major chosen inside the same admitted cohort (major selection happens in the second semester of sophomore year). Once affiliated, ECE gives a hardware-and-signals core (circuits, digital logic, signals, embedded) with a required Culminating Design Experience and hands-on robotics through ECE 4160 Fast Robots, which focuses on 'systems level design and implementation of fast and dynamic autonomous robots' and has students 'design a fast autonomous car, explore dynamic behaviors, acting forces, sensors, and reactive control on an embedded processor'. The costs are a modest affiliation gate (C+ in gateway courses, 2.5 GPA) and the fact that ECE has no formal robotics track — robotics is a listed concentration area rather than a defined thread.
ece.notable: First-years arrive without an official major inside Cornell Engineering and must be 'accepted into and affiliate with a specific Engineering major' (CORNELL-E2). ECE 4160 Fast Robots is cross-listed with ECE 5160, MAE 4190 and MAE 5190, so the robotics course is shared with mechanical engineering (CORNELL-E4). The College of Engineering is now named the Cornell David A. Duffield College of Engineering (CORNELL-E2).

why_us_ammunition: Bass Connections year-long interdisciplinary project teams are open to all current Duke undergraduates, typically run 9-12 months with 5-15 undergraduate and graduate students plus at least two faculty leaders, meet weekly, and carry ~12 hours/week and academic credit — a concrete vehicle for an AI/robotics applicant to name a specific team and theme [DUKE-S5][DUKE-S8].

Pratt's undergraduate research pipeline is explicit and early: experiential learning begins in the first semester, faculty labs post undergraduate openings in the Muser system across three recruiting rounds per year, first- and second-year students can take an EGR independent study as a free elective, and the Pratt Research Fellows Program supports three semesters of immersive research [DUKE-S4].

Duke Robotics sits in Pratt: undergraduate courses in robotics and autonomy are offered through Mechanical Engineering & Materials Science, and many students take robotics projects as their senior design capstone or as independent study with robotics faculty [DUKE-S7].

Duke's surgical-robotics ecosystem (the NSF-funded Traineeship in the Advancement of Surgical Technologies) shows a research direction an applicant interested in AI plus medical robotics can point to as a long-term goal [DUKE-S7].

Because Duke publishes no separate Trinity vs. Pratt admit rate and the 'Why Duke' essay explicitly asks how you will engage with Trinity or Pratt, naming the specific school and a named lab/team is the highest-leverage move available [DUKE-S1][DUKE-S3].

door.easier_than_cs_basis: Duke's Class of 2029 profile publishes only a single university-wide funnel (58,712 applications, 5.2% overall, 12.6% Early Decision, 4.2% Regular Decision) with no Trinity-versus-Pratt breakdown, so no per-college or per-major comparison is published (DUKE-E6).

ece.vs_cs: At Duke, ECE is the only door to robotics hardware: the BSE curriculum forces circuits, digital systems, signals and controls (ECE 110L/230L/250D/270DL/280L) and then lets you stack the ECE Machine Learning concentration on top, so you graduate able to build the sensing-and-actuation stack as well as the model (DUKE-E1, DUKE-E2). CS in Trinity gives more algorithms, theory and software breadth and a lighter math/lab load, but no accredited engineering degree and no required hardware sequence. The real cost is structural, not curricular: choosing ECE means applying to Pratt rather than Trinity on the application itself, and Duke publishes no evidence that either college is the easier admit (DUKE-E4, DUKE-E6).
ece.notable: Duke offers a university-wide Minor in Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence administered by ECE (DUKE-E8), an ECE minor, and a Robotics and Automation Certificate that pairs ECE 383 with ME 555 Robot Studio plus machine-learning, controls/dynamics and ethics courses (DUKE-E7). Pratt awards BSE degrees in Biomedical, Civil, Environmental, Mechanical and Electrical & Computer engineering only (DUKE-E5).

admissions.admit_rate_note: Fall 2025: 66,881 applicants, 8,921 admitted, 4,071 enrolled = 13.34% [GT-S1]. In-state (Georgia) 3,691/12,527 = 29.5%; out-of-state 4,513/44,596 = 10.1%; international 716/9,758 = 7.3% [GT-S1] (INFERRED - division of CDS C1 counts). Georgia Tech's own published Fall 2025 profile rounds these to 30% Georgia / 9% non-Georgia [GT-S10][GT-S11]; the Fall 2026 profile shows 67,985 applications, 8,715 admits, 28% Georgia / 9% non-Georgia, class goal 4,100 [GT-S9]. For a North Carolina resident the operative number is the ~9-10% non-resident rate, not the 13.3% headline.
admissions.major_admit_context: Georgia Tech admits by major, and the college you name on the Common App materially changes your odds. Institute-published profiles show only intended-area-of-study mix rather than per-college admit rates: 42% Engineering, 15% Computing, 22% Sciences, 7% Business, 8% Liberal Arts, 6% Design for the Fall 2026 admitted class [GT-S9] (Fall 2025: 44% Engineering, 16% Computing) [GT-S10]. The College of Computing states only that 'Competition remains high, with an admission rate for Computing that is lower than Georgia Tech's already low overall admission rate,' while disclosing that the Fall 2025 cycle drew 66,895 total applications including 13,711 for CS and Computational Media combined, that 1,547 first-year students were offered admission to CS or CM, and that CS alone accounted for 92.7% of College applicants [GT-S8]. That implies a CS+CM admit rate of roughly 11.3% (INFERRED - 1,547/13,711) [GT-S8], i.e. computing sits below the Institute-wide 13.3% [GT-S1]. The widely repeated figures of 8.5% for the College of Computing versus 13.1% for the College of Engineering could NOT be verified from any Georgia Tech source fetched on 2026-08-16 - treat them as unsourced. The second, larger constraint is mobility after admission: change of major into CS was suspended, and as of April 15, 2025 the College of Computing 'updated their change of major process based on semester of matriculation,' with separate rules for students who matriculated in summer 2024 or afterward; the department 'is now prepared to begin accepting Change of Major applications again on a limited basis, which includes students who would like to add Computer Science as a second major' [GT-S7][GT-S8]. Practical consequence: apply directly to the major you want (Computer Science, or a specific engineering major such as Mechanical Engineering); do not plan on entering through another major and switching. Note also that Georgia Tech's CDS marks 'state residency' as Very Important in the review [GT-S1], which is the single biggest structural headwind for a North Carolina applicant.

admissions.ea_admit_rate_note: CDS C22 confirms a non-restrictive Early Action plan (closing 11/1, notification 1/31) but publishes no EA applicant/admit counts, and no Georgia Tech page fetched on 2026-08-16 published an EA2 admit rate [GT-S1][GT-S3]. The frequently cited 8.1% EA2 rate could not be verified from an official source.

admissions.gpa_note: 95.85% of enrolled first-year students reported a weighted GPA of 4.0 or higher; average high school GPA 4.17 with 95.31% submitting GPA [GT-S1]. Class rank: 88.69% in the top tenth, 97.93% in the top quarter, though only 40.43% of enrollees submitted rank [GT-S1].
admissions.test_policy_2027_cycle: REQUIRED. CDS C8 for the 2025-2026 edition states SAT/ACT are 'Required to be considered for admission' for Fall 2027 [GT-S1], and the admissions site states 'All first-year applicants must submit results from at least one SAT and/or ACT in order to be considered for admission' [GT-S4]. Self-reported scores are accepted and recommended (Common App testing section or the post-submission portal form); scores on transcripts or sent by email/fax/mail are not used. ACT writing and the SAT optional essay are not required. Highest section scores are combined (English/Math/Reading for ACT; EBRW/Math for SAT). CLT scores may be self-reported but do not substitute for SAT/ACT [GT-S4]. Latest acceptable test date per CDS C8E: 23 January [GT-S1].

why_us_ammunition: Institute for Robotics and Intelligent Machines (IRIM) is Georgia Tech's cross-campus robotics institute whose mission is 'to ignite collaborations across Georgia Tech and beyond to imagine, design, and deploy robotic systems that enhance human capabilities to sense, think, and act' - a natural hook for a FIRST/robotics applicant [GT-S12].

Scale and selectivity of the computing pipeline is itself a talking point: 13,711 applications for CS and Computational Media in one cycle, with CS accounting for 92.7% of College of Computing applicants and 1,547 admits [GT-S8] - showing you understand what you are applying into strengthens a 'why this major' answer.

Georgia Tech's admitted-class mix (42% Engineering, 15% Computing in Fall 2026) means interdisciplinary robotics arguments that connect Mechanical Engineering and Computing land well with a reader [GT-S9].

Because change of major into CS is only reopening 'on a limited basis' [GT-S7], an essay that commits credibly to one named major (and explains why that specific curriculum) reads as informed rather than opportunistic.

State residency is Very Important in Georgia Tech's own review [GT-S1]; a non-Georgia applicant needs the essays and activity record to carry more weight, so lead with concrete robotics artifacts (build, code, competition outcomes) rather than generic enthusiasm.

However, on your Common Application, you are asked to select an intended (primary) major' — and 'consideration of your major is an important part of our application review process' (GT-E3).

computing.basis: Georgia Tech admits by major, and the college you name on the Common App materially changes your odds. Institute-published profiles show only intended-area-of-study mix rather than per-college admit rates: 42% Engineering, 15% Computing, 22% Sciences, 7% Business, 8% Liberal Arts, 6% Design for the Fall 2026 admitted class [GT-S9] (Fall 2025: 44% Engineering, 16% Computing) [GT-S10]. The College of Computing states only that 'Competition remains high, with an admission rate for Computing that is lower than Georgia Tech's already low overall admission rate,' while disclosing that the Fall 2025 cycle drew 66,895 total applications including 13,711 for CS and Computational Media combined, that 1,547 first-year students were offered admission to CS or CM, and that CS alone accounted for 92.7% of College applicants [GT-S8]. That implies a CS+CM admit rate of roughly 11.3% (INFERRED - 1,547/13,711) [GT-S8], i.e. computing sits below the Institute-wide 13.3% [GT-S1]. The widely repeated figures of 8.5% for the College of Computing versus 13.1% for the College of Engineering could NOT be verified from any Georgia Tech source fetched on 2026-08-16 - treat them as unsourced. The second, larger constraint is mobility after admission: change of major into CS was suspended, and as of April 15, 2025 the College of Computing 'updated their change of major process based on semester of matriculation,' with separate rules for students who matriculated in summer 2024 or afterward; the department 'is now prepared to begin accepting Change of Major applications again on a limited basis, which includes students who would like to add Computer Science as a second major' [GT-S7][GT-S8]. Practical consequence: apply directly to the major you want (Computer Science, or a specific engineering major such as Mechanical Engineering); do not plan on entering through another major and switching. Note also that Georgia Tech's CDS marks 'state residency' as Very Important in the review [GT-S1], which is the single biggest structural headwind for a North Carolina applicant.

door.how_you_enter: 'When you apply to Georgia Tech as a first-year applicant, you do not apply to a specific major or college. However, on your Common Application, you are asked to select an intended (primary) major' — and 'consideration of your major is an important part of our application review process' (GT-E3).
door.easier_than_cs_basis: Georgia Tech does not publish admit rates by major or college (the first-year class profile page returned no such figures), so no numeric ECE-vs-CS comparison exists. The documented asymmetry is post-admission: 'Due to high-demand, first-year students who are admitted Summer 2024 and beyond will not have the option to confirm their major to the BS in Computer Science' (GT-E4), and the registrar states such students 'will not have the option to change their major to the BS in Computer Science and must plan accordingly' (GT-E5).
door.internal_gate: No published GPA or capacity gate to confirm an ECE major; the restriction runs the other way — CS is a 'space-restricted program' now accepting change-of-major applications only 'on a limited basis', and 'Students should not assume they will be able to change their major to Computer Science' (GT-E7).

ece.vs_cs: At Georgia Tech ECE and CS sit in different colleges (College of Engineering vs College of Computing) and, because major confirmation into the BS CS is closed to students admitted Summer 2024 and later, ECE is the door that stays open — you can confirm or change into EE or Computer Engineering, but not into CS. The ECE thread system is unusually well matched to this applicant: BS EE picks any two of eight threads including Robotics, and BS CmpE picks two of nine including Robotics & Autonomous Systems, backed by ECE 3550/4550 controls, ECE 4560 robotics, ECE 4580 vision, ECE 4252 machine learning and ECE 4180 embedded systems. The cost is that GT publishes no admit-rate evidence, and intended major is explicitly weighed in review, so listing ECE is a real commitment rather than a backdoor.
ece.notable: Georgia Tech CS is CAC-accredited while EE and CmpE are EAC-accredited under the electrical/computer program criteria (GT-E1). ECE also owns robotics-specific graduate courses (ECE 7785 Introduction to Robotics Research, ECE 8741 Robotics Capstone Project) that undergraduates can approach through the BS/MS (GT-E6).

score_notes.cs_foundations: 17 required core credits (Gateway, 601.220 Intermediate Programming, 601.226 Data Structures, 601.229 Computer System Fundamentals, 601.433 Intro Algorithms) at C+ or higher, plus a required discrete-math/theory option [JHU-S1].
score_notes.math_foundations: Only 16 math credits are required and linear algebra plus Calculus III are listed as recommended*, not required, even though they are hard prerequisites for 601.475 Machine Learning [JHU-S1][JHU-S2].
score_notes.ai_curriculum_breadth: The catalog lists 400-level undergraduate courses spanning AI, ML, learning theory, deep learning, RL, vision, NLP, robotics, causal inference, HCI and AI safety [JHU-S2].
score_notes.ai_curriculum_depth: Every graduate AI course numbered 601.6xx has a 400-level undergraduate twin, so undergraduates reach graduate content directly (e.g., 601.482/682 Deep Learning) [JHU-S2].
score_notes.emerging_ai_topics: Named 400-level courses include Artificial Agents (601.470), NLP: Self-Supervised Models (601.471), AI Safety Alignment & Governance (601.469), Embodied AI with Web-Scale Video Data (601.460) and Generative Vision (601.483) [JHU-S2].
score_notes.curricular_flexibility: Of 120 credits, about 64 are required in-field (40 CS + 16 math + 8 science) and only 12 upper-level CS credits are mandated, leaving large elective room [JHU-S1].
score_notes.course_availability: The Spring 2026 schedule confirms 601.464, 601.474 and 601.475 ran with meeting times, but no fetched page documents the rotation of newer electives such as 601.470 Artificial Agents [JHU-S5].
score_notes.undergraduate_research_access: Official participation claims range from 65% to over 90%, but an official HOUR deck states 80% of undergraduate researchers are entirely uncompensated volunteers [JHU-S13][JHU-S15][JHU-S38].
score_notes.faculty_mentorship: The 9:1 student-faculty ratio and 22 new DSAI faculty hired in August 2025 expand capacity, but HOUR's own guidance is cold-email outreach with 3-4 follow-ups [JHU-S25][JHU-S8][JHU-S38].
score_notes.project_based_learning: Only one CSCI-TEAM course (3-4 credits) is required and it "may overlap with other requirements"; there is no single named senior capstone [JHU-S1].
score_notes.robotics_autonomy_options: Robotics Minor; 13 undergrad robotics courses. 17 labs, LCSR, 1 competition team.
score_notes.computing_resources: Rockfish offers 45,072 cores and 32 A100/L40S GPU nodes, but accounts activate only after a PI with an approved allocation adds the user [JHU-S32][JHU-S33].
score_notes.industry_preparation: University-wide 91% are employed full-time or in graduate school within six months, but no CS-specific placement or salary data is published [JHU-S16][JHU-S1].
score_notes.graduate_school_preparation: 38% of graduates continue to graduate/professional school and the Senior Honors Thesis (601.519/520) unlocks extra research credit toward the major [JHU-S16][JHU-S1].
score_notes.fourplusone_quality: Concurrent BS/MSE students receive a Dean's Master's Fellowship covering half of full-time tuition after four years at JHU, plus two double-counted courses under WSE policy [JHU-S17][JHU-S18].
score_notes.intellectual_energy: HopHacks runs every semester and its September 12-14, 2025 edition drew nearly 300 participants from 57 universities with a record 102 projects [JHU-S21].
score_notes.healthy_ambition: No current multi-source student evidence on competitiveness or pressure was collected, and the brief forbids inferring it from structure.
score_notes.student_agency: A CS major can declare via an SIS request plus an advisor-approved four-year plan, and can substitute a 600-level course for a 400-level one in the robotics minor without an exception form [JHU-S1][JHU-S3].
score_notes.community_within_scale: 5,679 full-time undergraduates with a mandatory two-year on-campus residency requirement and 93% of first-years in college housing [JHU-S25][JHU-S26].
score_notes.technical_club_ecosystem: The CS department lists nine student groups including HopAI (the AI society), a Data Science Club, ACM with a Systems Programming subgroup, Cyberbirds, Game Dev Society and WiCS [JHU-S20].
score_notes.nonacademic_club_variety: About 80% of students are involved in one or more student organization, but no full student-activities directory was fetched to verify breadth [JHU-S27].
score_notes.non_greek_social_life: 25% of men and 21% of women join Greek organizations per the 2025-26 CDS, and the two-year residency requirement keeps underclass housing outside Greek control [JHU-S25][JHU-S26].
score_notes.campus_engagement: 93% of first-year students live on campus but only 46% of all undergraduates do, so most juniors and seniors live in surrounding neighborhoods [JHU-S25].
score_notes.recreation_facilities: The O'Connor Center is free to all Homewood students and includes a six-lane pool, climbing wall and bouldering cave, indoor track and three weight rooms, though it closes 3-4 weeks a year for maintenance [JHU-S29][JHU-S31].
score_notes.daily_life: A single contiguous Homewood campus with a two-year residency requirement, on-campus rec center at the North Gate, and off-campus housing within walking distance [JHU-S43][JHU-S28].

admissions.admit_rate_note_reason: JHU publishes no state-residency admit-rate split in CDS Section C (state residency is marked 'Not Considered' in C7).
admissions.major_admit_context: JHU's CDS reports one undergraduate funnel for the Homewood schools (50,259 / 3,072) with no separate Whiting School of Engineering vs. Krieger School of Arts & Sciences rates, and — critically — its ED figures are reported as a single combined round: CDS C21 lists both an ED I closing date of 11/1 (notification 12/11) and an ED II closing date of 1/3 (notification 2/12) but reports only one pair of counts (7,639 applied / 835 admitted = 10.93%), i.e. ED I and ED II are COMBINED and cannot be separated [JHU-S1]. The only place JHU differentiates by division is testing policy, where CDS C8 reads "Required to be considered for admission (Homewood Schools); Not required but considered if submitted (Peabody Conservatory)" [JHU-S1].

supplemental_essays.prompt: "At Johns Hopkins, community is built through dialogue, collaboration, and a willingness to engage across differences. Whether on campus or in the broader world, community depends on bridge builders who can listen to differing perspectives, challenge their own assumptions, or work together toward shared goals. Drawing on your own experiences, what have you learned about engaging across differences and how has it shaped the way you think about building bridges, enhancing community, and working with others?"

why_us_ammunition: The Laboratory for Computational Sensing and Robotics (LCSR) describes itself as "one of the most technologically advanced robotics research centers worldwide... an international leader in the areas of medical robotics, autonomous systems, and bio-inspiration" — the single strongest anchor for a robotics applicant's Hopkins essay [JHU-S4].

LCSR is deliberately cross-divisional, joining Whiting School engineers with researchers from the School of Medicine, Bloomberg School of Public Health, Krieger School of Arts & Sciences, the Applied Physics Laboratory and Kennedy Krieger Institute — a genuine 'only at Hopkins' structural fact [JHU-S4].

Named sub-labs let you be specific: PULSE (photoacoustic/ultrasound imaging with robots), HAMR (haptics and medical robotics), CIRL (computational interaction and robotics), LIMBS (locomotion in mechanical and biological systems), and MUSiiC (interventional ultrasound) [JHU-S5].

LCSR's faculty roster spans CS, mechanical engineering, ECE and clinical departments (e.g., Russell Taylor in computer-integrated interventional medicine; Axel Krieger's IMERSE lab on autonomous surgical robots; Iulian Iordachita's AMIRo lab on smart surgical tools) — useful for naming a specific mentor fit [JHU-S7][JHU-S8].

Because the 2026-27 supplement is a single 350-word community/bridge-building prompt rather than a 'why Hopkins' essay, robotics specifics should be woven into a collaboration narrative (e.g., FRC team dynamics) rather than listed as a program wish list [JHU-S3].

door.how_you_enter: There is no ECE admission door: 'When you applied to Hopkins, you applied to the full university, and not to a specific school or major (except in the case of biomedical engineering)' and 'You are not bound to the major you listed on your application' (JHU-E2).
door.easier_than_cs_basis: Identical door by policy. JHU admits university-wide and Biomedical Engineering is the only major with its own admission decision, so ECE and CS applicants receive the same admission review and either can declare after matriculating (JHU-E2).
door.internal_gate: No published GPA or capacity gate to declare Electrical Engineering or Computer Engineering; students may choose any major across Krieger and Whiting after matriculation (JHU-E2). The LCSR Robotics Minor requires grades of C- or higher, a minimum of 6 courses and 18 credits, with at least 6 credits outside the primary major department (JHU-E3).

ece.vs_cs: Johns Hopkins is the batch's cleanest 'no separate door' case in the applicant's favor: admission is university-wide with BME as the sole direct-admit exception, so ECE is neither easier nor harder than CS — you get in and then choose. That makes the decision purely about content, and ECE is strong here: EN.520.353/454 control systems, EN.520.241 mechatronics (teams design, build and demonstrate a robotic system), EN.520.465 Machine Perception, EN.520.438 Deep Learning, plus a two-semester capstone. The multiplier is the Laboratory for Computational Sensing and Robotics: its Robotics Minor is 'not owned by any one department' and 'Any student from any department within the university can work toward the minor', so an ECE major can add a transcript-recognized robotics credential built on kinematics/dynamics, systems-and-control and computation-and-sensing.
ece.notable: Whiting's accreditation page lists Electrical Engineering and Computer Engineering as separately EAC-accredited BS programs, while Computer Science is accredited by the Computing Accreditation Commission (JHU-E4). The robotics minor requires at least 6 of the 18 credits outside the student's primary major department, so it forces ECE students into robotics coursework beyond their home department (JHU-E3). EN.620.745 Seminar in Computational Sensing and Robotics is cross-listed into the ECE catalog (JHU-E1).

admissions.admit_rate_note: Fall 2025: 67,101 applicants, 30,218 admitted, 6,559 enrolled = 45.0% [UMD-S1]. In-state 8,075/18,487 = 43.7%; out-of-state 22,143/48,614 = 45.6% [UMD-S1] (INFERRED - division of CDS C1 counts). This is COUNTERINTUITIVE - UMD's reported out-of-state admit rate (45.6%) is slightly HIGHER than its in-state rate (43.7%) in the 2025-2026 CDS, the reverse of every other public in this batch; no UMD narrative page fetched on 2026-08-16 explains or contradicts it, so treat the residency gap as effectively neutral rather than favorable and re-check next year's CDS. Waitlist: 247 offered, 0 accepted a place [UMD-S1].
admissions.major_admit_context: UMD separates admission to the university from admission to the major through Limited Enrollment Programs (LEPs). The LEP list includes both majors a robotics applicant cares about - Computer Science and Engineering - alongside Biochemistry, Biological Sciences, Business, Chemistry, Criminology, Immersive Media Design, Neuroscience and Psychology [UMD-S5]. The mechanics: 'Prospective students should indicate their preferred major when completing their online application... However, your preferred major does not affect your admissibility to the university. Admitted students who selected an LEP as their major are reviewed by the specific program to determine admission to that major,' and 'While the majority of students are admitted to their preferred major, some LEP applicants may not be.' Students admitted to UMD but not to the LEP are placed in Letters & Sciences to meet gateway requirements, while non-LEP applicants 'are admitted directly to the major indicated on their application'; all major decisions arrive in the admission decision letter [UMD-S5][UMD-S3]. LEP review is also test-optional [UMD-S7]. If you land in Letters & Sciences, the CS gateway for students starting Fall 2024 or later is concrete and demanding: CMSC131 or CMSC133 with a minimum B-, CMSC132 with a minimum B-, MATH140 with a minimum B-, and a minimum 3.0 GPA across all institutions, with the final grade posted by the application deadline; starting at CMSC131/133 means 'a minimum of 7 semesters/terms to complete the major' [UMD-S6]. No public per-major admit rate or internal-transfer slot count (the often-quoted '~100 CS slots per year') appears on any UMD page fetched on 2026-08-16 - that figure is unverified. Practical consequence: naming CS or Engineering costs nothing at the university level (preferred major does not affect admissibility) but the major decision is a second, program-level gate, and the fallback path through Letters & Sciences is a real risk with a 3.0/B- floor.

why_us_ammunition: The Maryland Robotics Center is the strongest single hook: 'an interdisciplinary research center in the Institute for Systems Research within the A. James Clark School of Engineering,' with '47 Faculty members from 8 different departments' and '26 State-of-the-art labs and facilities including 3 multi-user MRC labs, 20 affiliated research labs, and 3 affiliated facilities,' spanning autonomous systems, bio-inspired, cognitive, extreme, human-robot interaction, medical, miniature and multirobot systems [UMD-S8].

MRC's named MATRIX Lab is pitched as 'Advancing Smarter, More Affordable Autonomy' and the center offers an undergraduate robotics minor alongside graduate options [UMD-S8] - a concrete undergraduate-accessible credential to name.

The Institute for Systems Research is 'a permanent, interdisciplinary research unit' that began as 'one of the National Science Foundation's original Engineering Research Centers in 1985' and now hosts 'more than 60 faculty and other researchers from 13 departments in five colleges' working on autonomous and distributed systems [UMD-S9].

There is a Clark School FIRST scholarship pathway specifically for FRC/FTC alumni requiring a 500-word essay on how FIRST shaped your career goals [UMD-S10] - your robotics record maps directly onto an institutional award, even if the cycle dates need confirming.

UMD's own framing rewards specificity: the required 300-word question asks for 'your reasons for wishing to enroll at UMD' [UMD-S4], and LEP review is a program-level read [UMD-S5], so naming MRC/ISR labs and the robotics minor does double duty.

door.how_you_enter: Two steps: you apply to and are admitted directly to the A. James Clark School of Engineering, which is itself a Limited Enrollment Program, and then you must clear the Clark School gateway review at 45 credits to continue in an engineering major such as ECE — 'All students accepted directly as freshman into the Clark School of Engineering must complete a series of gateway courses and a review at 45 credits.'
door.easier_than_cs_basis: Maryland runs ECE and CS under two different Limited Enrollment Programs with different severities, and the published requirements differ sharply. The Clark School engineering LEP gateway for newly admitted freshmen requires, by the semester they reach their 45th UMD credit: ENGL 101; ENES 100 (C-); MATH 141 (C- or AP); PHYS 161 (C- or AP); CHEM 135/271/134 (C- or AP); one Distributive Studies Gen-Ed; and a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.00, with only one repeat of any single course allowed. Computer Science is a separate LEP whose published gateway standard is materially higher — the CS minor gateway effective spring 2025 requires CMSC131/133/141 at B-, CMSC132/142 at B-, MATH140 at B- and a 3.0 UMD GPA. A 2.00 continuation GPA for engineering versus B- course grades and a 3.0 GPA for the CS side is the published gap.
door.internal_gate: Clark School LEP gateway review at 45 credits (courses and 2.00 cumulative GPA above, one repeat maximum per course). Beyond that, ECE imposes a course-level control: 'Departmental permission is required in order for students to register and for all courses in the major.' The BSEE also requires a grade of C- or higher in all engineering, mathematics and science courses and their prerequisites. No separate ECE-specific admission gate beyond the Clark School LEP was found on the pages fetched.

ece.vs_cs: At Maryland the whole Clark School is one Limited Enrollment Program, so ECE inherits an engineering-wide gateway (2.00 cumulative GPA plus five specified courses at C- by 45 credits) rather than a department-specific competition, while Computer Science is a separate and stiffer LEP whose published gateway standards run to B- course grades and a 3.0 GPA. ECE gives you a full controls stack (ENEE460/461/463/469), a dedicated ENEE467 Robotics Project Laboratory, ENEE436 Foundations of Machine Learning and ENEE408 Capstone Design — arguably a more complete robotics path than CS at this school. The cost is the absence of a named robotics concentration in the BSEE and the department's requirement that you get departmental permission to register for major courses.
ece.notable: Maryland ECE offers a distinct Cyber-Physical Systems Engineering BS, separately EAC-accredited, whose junior/senior sequence includes ENEB346 Linear Algebra for Machine Learning Applications and ENEB408A/B Capstone Design I/II — this is effectively a purpose-built embedded/autonomy degree and is unusual among the schools in this batch. ECE also offers a Quantum Science and Engineering minor and an ECE Honors Program (honors students may apply up to 6 ENEE499/499L credits versus 5 for others).

admissions.admit_rate_note_note: Michigan's CDS does not publish in-state vs out-of-state application or admit counts, even though CDS C7 marks state residency as 'Considered'.
admissions.major_admit_context: Michigan's binding constraint is the Computer Science major, not the college. U-M's CSE department states: 'Due to capacity constraints, students who are admitted to the University of Michigan in Fall 2023 or later must first be selected for the Computer Science (CS) major before they can declare the major. This selection policy ... is the same for students in both the College of Engineering and the College of Literature, Science, and the Arts (LSA). The selection policy applies only to the CS major and does NOT apply to students seeking to major in the Computer Engineering (CE) or Data Science (DS) programs' [UMICH-S6]. Incoming students request CS 'advance selection' on the Common Application itself, and transfer students cannot switch into CS once on campus [UMICH-S6][UMICH-S7]. Robotics is the opposite story: the Robotics BSE has no capacity cap — students declare after at least one term with a 2.0 GPA [UMICH-S8]. So a robotics-focused applicant should target Robotics BSE (open declaration) and treat CS as the gated option requiring the advance-selection request on the application.
admissions.ed_admit_rate_note: Early Decision is brand new — U-M describes it as 'New for 2025-2026 Application Cycle ... new option to apply Early Decision (binding decision)'. The Fall 2025 CDS therefore reports no ED plan and no ED counts. No ED admit rate exists yet.
admissions.ea_admit_rate_note: CDS C22 confirms a non-binding, non-restrictive Early Action plan closing November 1 with notification January 31, but U-M does not report EA application or admit counts.
admissions.sat_mid50_note: Fall 2025 CDS C9: 25th 1370 / 50th 1470 / 75th 1530, from 4,503 enrolled submitters.
admissions.pct_submitting_sat_note: 55% of enrolled first-years submitted SAT scores; 18% submitted ACT scores.
admissions.gpa_note: CDS C12 average high school GPA 3.9, reported for 97.8% of enrolled first-years; CDS C11 shows 38.8% of enrolled first-years with a 4.0 GPA. CDS C7 marks class rank 'Not Considered'.
admissions.test_policy_note: This one is genuinely ambiguous and worth verifying. CDS C8 marks SAT/ACT 'Recommended' for the Fall 2027 cycle (not 'test-optional'), and CDS C7 rates test scores 'Important' — a stronger weighting than most peers. Meanwhile U-M's admissions and LSA pages say test-optional only 'for the 2026 application cycle'. There is no published Fall 2027 test-policy statement, so the practical read is test-optional-but-recommended, with scores carrying real weight when submitted.

interview.mechanism: By invitation and program-specific. U-M's CDS C7 note reads: 'Some applicants to Music, Theatre and Dance and some applicants to the College of Engineering may be interviewed. A portfolio is required and considered for admission for Art, Architecture and the Ross Business School.' The top-level C7 grid still marks Interview 'Not Considered', so a College of Engineering interview should be treated as possible but neither required nor requestable.

first_frc_scholarship.note: No FIRST/FRC-specific scholarship is published on umich.edu. The College of Engineering states that its merit scholarships are awarded automatically with no separate application, which leaves no mechanism for an activity-specific FIRST award.

The Ford Motor Company Robotics Building, completed in 2021, is a $75 million, 134,000-square-foot facility and Ford's first robotics and mobility lab on a university campus, with roughly 100 Ford researchers on its fourth floor [UMICH-S9].

door.how_you_enter: You apply to the University of Michigan / College of Engineering, enter undeclared, and then declare: 'Undergraduate students apply to the University of Michigan for admission. Once admitted as a student and maintaining an appropriate academic record, you may declare a major in electrical engineering or computer engineering after talking with an advisor' (UMICH-E2).
door.easier_than_cs_basis: Published policy difference rather than admit rates: Michigan requires CS applicants to be selected into the major at the application stage — 'students who apply for admission into the College of LSA or the College of Engineering and are considering computer science as a major must now request selection into the major on the Common Application' (UMICH-E3) — while the CSE department states 'Students are not required to request advance selection for the computer engineering and data science major programs' (UMICH-E5). Per-major admit rates are not published.
door.internal_gate: First-years enter the College of Engineering undeclared and are urged to declare by the start of their third term; declaring EE or Computer Engineering requires only 'maintaining an appropriate academic record' plus an advisor conversation, with no published GPA threshold or capacity cap (UMICH-E2).

ece.vs_cs: Michigan is the batch's strongest example of ECE being a genuinely less-gated door: EE and Computer Engineering are declared after enrollment with no advance selection, whereas CS applicants must request selection into the major on the Common Application and can be admitted to Michigan without getting CS. The ECE division's own course set is unusually deep in robotics — EECS 367 Intro to Autonomous Robotics, 464 Hands-on Robotics, 465 Algorithmic Robotics, 467 Autonomous Robotics Design Experience, 568 Mobile Robotics, plus 360/461 controls and 442/445 vision and ML. The trade is that CS in Engineering is not ABET-accredited by EAC anyway, so choosing EE or CompE also buys you EAC accreditation that the CS B.S.E. does not carry.
ece.notable: EE and CS live in one EECS department split into an ECE Division and a CSE Division, so ECE students sit inside the same department as CS. The College of Engineering bulletin lists Computer Engineering and Electrical Engineering as EAC-accredited while the B.S.E. in Computer Science is not EAC-accredited (UMICH-E1). Computer Engineering and Data Science are the CSE-side programs that do not require advance selection (UMICH-E5).

score_notes.cs_foundations: Required core includes CSC 226 discrete math, CSC 316 data structures/algorithms, CSC 333 automata and computability, CSC 246 OS, CSC 230 C/tools and a 4-credit CSC 326 software engineering — a complete theory+systems spine, ABET-accredited [NCSU-S1][NCSU-S2].
score_notes.math_foundations: Three-semester calculus (MA 141/241/242), MA 305 linear algebra and ST 370 probability/statistics are all required; optimization is elective only [NCSU-S1].
score_notes.ai_curriculum_breadth: CSC 411 AI and CSC 422 ML are required and CSC 201/301 come early, but no undergraduate CSC course for computer vision, NLP, RL or deep learning was found on the concentration's elective lists [NCSU-S1].
score_notes.ai_curriculum_depth: 21 hours of AI coursework with 15 hours of AI-directed electives, but the graduate versions (e.g., CSC 522) are open only to CSC Honors or ABM students [NCSU-S1][NCSU-S15].
score_notes.emerging_ai_topics: CSC 455 Social Computing and Decentralized AI and CSC 484 Building Game AI are catalog electives and DSA micro-courses cover applied ML, but no LLM/generative-AI/agents course was verified [NCSU-S1][NCSU-S9].
score_notes.curricular_flexibility: The 121-hour AI concentration leaves only about 3 hours of truly free electives after chemistry, physics, calculus and the CS core [NCSU-S1][NCSU-S6].
score_notes.course_availability: CSC 411 and CSC 422 are required and therefore scheduled every year, but CSC 490/491/499 are majors-only and CSC 492 requires 6 prior CSC restricted-elective hours [NCSU-S1][NCSU-S18].
score_notes.undergraduate_research_access: CSC 299 exists specifically for first- and second-year undergraduate research and the department runs faculty Lightning Talks the first Friday of each semester, though OUR funding caps at $500 supplies + $1,000 of work [NCSU-S13][NCSU-S11].
score_notes.faculty_mentorship: Named faculty coordinators for each elective track and honors program plus a recurring department-run mentor-matching event [NCSU-S15][NCSU-S14][NCSU-S13].
score_notes.project_based_learning: CSC 492 Senior Design is a required team-built software system with written and oral reports, run through the Senior Design Center with industrial sponsors [NCSU-S3][NCSU-S18].
score_notes.robotics_autonomy_options: Joint NC State / UNC Asheville B.S. in Engineering (EAC); 9 undergrad robotics courses. 6 labs, CRIM, 2 competition teams.
score_notes.computing_resources: No page documenting undergraduate GPU or HPC cluster access was retrieved this session.
score_notes.industry_preparation: 548 new co-op rotations and 30 career fairs in 2025-26 with 70% of undergraduates completing an internship, plus a required industry-sponsored capstone — but no salary or employer data is published [NCSU-S30][NCSU-S3].
score_notes.graduate_school_preparation: CSC Honors requires a completed CSC 498/499 with a written report and permits 5XX graduate coursework, but no undergraduate publication or PhD-placement evidence was found [NCSU-S14][NCSU-S15].
score_notes.fourplusone_quality: ABM double-counts up to 12 graduate credits into an AI-capable MS (CSC 520 AI I is a core option) finishing within 12-18 months, gated at a 3.500 GPA with no published funding discount [NCSU-S19][NCSU-S32].
score_notes.intellectual_energy: Hack_NCState drew a 24-hour, free, cross-disciplinary field into Talley's State Ballroom in February 2026 and HackPack ran a CTF in April 2026 [NCSU-S22a][NCSU-S23].
score_notes.healthy_ambition: Major grade rules are permissive (C/C- minimums, 2.0 major-GPA floor), but CODA forces first-year competition for capacity-limited CS seats judged on chemistry, physics and calculus grades [NCSU-S1][NCSU-S4].
score_notes.student_agency: CSC 299/490/499 proposals, three concentrations and three elective tracks give real choice, yet graduate courses are restricted to Honors/ABM students and AI students are barred from the Robotics Track [NCSU-S13][NCSU-S15].
score_notes.community_within_scale: CSC Honors, ABM, robotics teams and HackPack provide sub-communities inside a College of Engineering of more than 12,500 students; the living-learning village roster was not retrievable [NCSU-S27][NCSU-S33].
score_notes.technical_club_ecosystem: Four separate technical organizations have dated 2025-26 activity: Hack_NCState (Feb 14-15, 2026), HackPack CTF (Apr 17-18, 2026), Aerial Robotics Club (2025-26 NC Space Grant award) and RoboPack [NCSU-S22a][NCSU-S23][NCSU-S25b][NCSU-S25c].
score_notes.nonacademic_club_variety: No student-organization directory or event calendar was fetched this session.
score_notes.non_greek_social_life: Official FSL data updated Summer 2026 shows 52 chapters and 3,800+ members at "more than 15%" of undergraduates, with Greek Village housing only 767 residents, so roughly 85% are unaffiliated and Greek life does not control housing [NCSU-S34].
score_notes.campus_engagement: No evidence was gathered on weekend/evening campus life, traditions, or residential versus commuter patterns.
score_notes.recreation_facilities: 430,000 sq ft across the Wellness and Recreation Center and Carmichael Gym with 11 indoor courts, an Olympic weightlifting room, the Casey Aquatic Center, a Climbing Center and an indoor track, included automatically in student fees [NCSU-S37][NCSU-S38].
score_notes.daily_life: Home-metro location with RDU and RTP nearby, 24-hour libraries Sunday-Thursday, and free staffed makerspaces — offset by a daily main-campus/Centennial-Campus split for CS students [NCSU-S24e][NCSU-S3][NCSU-S37].

admissions.overall_admit_rate_note: Fall 2024: 44,043 applied / 18,201 admitted / 5,837 enrolled. NC State has not posted a 2025-26 CDS, so this is the most recent official cycle. Waitlist: 9,704 offered a place, 4,194 accepted it, 261 admitted from it.
admissions.admit_rate_note: IN-STATE vs OUT-OF-STATE (Fall 2024, CDS): North Carolina residents 21,636 applied / 10,570 admitted = 48.9%. Out-of-state 19,487 applied / 6,963 admitted = 35.7%. International 2,920 applied / 668 admitted = 22.9%. The in-state advantage is roughly 13 percentage points, and it is policy-driven: UNC System Policy 700.1.3 caps nonresidents at 18 percent of NC State's fall first-time undergraduate class, with a State operating budget reduction if the cap is exceeded for two consecutive fiscal years.
admissions.major_admit_context: For engineering, NC State's intended major is explicitly non-competitive at the admission stage: 'All first-year students are admitted to the Engineering First Year Program (EFY). Students who know which engineering major they plan to pursue may indicate it on the admissions application as their intended major ... Please note that indication of an intended major on the admissions application has no effect whatsoever on admissions decisions.' Students must complete English composition, calculus, chemistry, physics and introductory engineering and computer courses before joining an academic department [NCSU-S6]. What is weighted heavily is the academic record: 'a student's high school academic record, including grade point average (weighted and unweighted) and class rank, receives significant emphasis in engineering admissions decisions', with the typical admitted first-year at an unweighted GPA of 3.8-4.0 [NCSU-S6]. Studio-based majors are the exception — College of Design, Fashion and Textile Design and Music Technology applicants must apply by November 1 with a 10-piece portfolio and an additional essay [NCSU-S2]. The CDS also flags a math floor: 'The most competitive applicants will have taken math through precalculus as a minimum in high school, particularly for STEM and business' [NCSU-S1].
admissions.ed_admit_rate_note: NC State offers no Early Decision plan (CDS C21 = No).
admissions.ea_admit_rate_note: CDS C22 confirms a non-binding Early Action plan closing November 1 with notification January 30, but NC State publishes no EA application or admit counts. NC State does say 'We don't necessarily give priority to early action applicants in the review process, but first-year early action applicants receive priority consideration for scholarships and financial aid' [NCSU-S2].
admissions.sat_mid50_note: Fall 2024 CDS C9: composite 25th 1290 / 50th 1360 / 75th 1440, from 1,422 enrolled submitters.
admissions.act_mid50_note: ACT composite 25th 25 / 50th 29 / 75th 32, from 2,365 enrolled submitters (41.34%) — NC State is one of the few schools in this set where ACT submission exceeds SAT submission.
admissions.pct_submitting_sat_note: 24.86% of enrolled first-years submitted SAT scores; 41.34% submitted ACT scores.
admissions.gpa_note: CDS C12 average high school GPA 3.83, reported for 98% of enrolled first-years; CDS C11 shows 20.02% with a 4.0 GPA and CDS C10 shows 40% in the top tenth of their class. The College of Engineering states the typical admitted first-year has an unweighted GPA of 3.8-4.0.
admissions.test_policy_note: Conditional test-optional with a GPA floor. CDS C8 states verbatim: 'We are test optional for applicants with a weighted GPA of 2.8 or above. International students for whom English is not their first language will be required to submit an English proficiency test.' The 2024-25 CDS labels these policies 'for use in admission for Fall 2026', with a latest receipt date of February 1, so Fall 2027 applicability is inferred from the standing UNC System-aligned rule. Applicants below a 2.8 weighted GPA must submit a score.
admissions.c7_note: CDS C7 also marks geographical residence and state residency 'Considered', consistent with the 18 percent nonresident cap.

interview.mechanism: No admissions interview is offered or considered; CDS C7 marks Interview 'Not Considered'. Portfolio review substitutes for studio-based majors (10-piece portfolio plus an additional essay, due November 1).

first_frc_scholarship.note: No FIRST/FRC-specific scholarship appears on NC State admissions, College of Engineering or student-services scholarship pages. NC State routes merit awards through the PackASSIST scholarship portal, which admitted students access after admission, with a February 15 priority consideration deadline; applying Early Action by November 1 gives priority consideration for scholarships. An FRC applicant should search PackASSIST after admission rather than expect a named FIRST award.

why_us_ammunition: NC State's College of Engineering states its robotics ambition directly: it 'aims to be a national leader in robotics innovation, focusing on AI-enabled, hands-on and collaborative robotics' [NCSU-S8].

Robotics at NC State is framed as bringing together 'control, AI, human interaction and systems integration from fundamentals to application' — language an FRC applicant can mirror when describing subsystem integration work [NCSU-S11].

The Engineering First Year Program means every engineering student shares a common first year before joining a department, so an applicant can honestly describe exploring across robotics-adjacent departments without gambling on a capped major [NCSU-S6].

For a North Carolina resident, the in-state admit rate was 48.9% versus 35.7% out-of-state, and NC residents who apply Early Action by November 1 and confirm residency by November 10 now receive decisions by the end of December — a genuine strategic advantage worth planning around [NCSU-S1][NCSU-S3].
Applying Early Action by November 1 is the only route to the University Honors Program application and gives priority consideration for scholarships and financial aid [NCSU-S2][NCSU-S3].

admissions.cs_gate_basis: All engineering first-years enter Engineering First-Year and compete through ranked CODA against per-department seat caps.

admission_structure.applies_to_note: major (engineering applicants are admitted into the Engineering First Year program)
units_named: Up to two majors are selected, each housed in one of the colleges: College of Agriculture and Life Sciences, College of Design, College of Education, College of Engineering, College of Humanities and Social Sciences, College of Natural Resources, College of Sciences, Wilson College of Textiles, Poole College of Management, plus University College/Exploratory Studies. Engineering entrants join the 'Engineering First Year Program (EFY)'.
admission_structure.internal_mobility: Post-enrollment major changes are 'on a space available basis'; engineering students move from EFY into a degree major through the college's placement process.

engineering.basis: CODA. The CODA GPA is computed from six Success courses (MA 141, MA 241, PY 205, PY 206, CH 101, CH 102), each of which must be passed with a C or better, and the CODA GPA must be at least 2.0; students must also complete ENG 101, E 101 and E 102 with C- or better and E 115 with an S. Requisites must be completed within four fall/spring semesters. 'Only students in the Engineering First Year program with a CODA GPA greater than or equal 2.0 and a continuation GPA of 2.0 will be guaranteed entrance into at least one of the remaining programs with available seats' — the guarantee is to a program with seats, not to your first choice. Practically, ECE gates course access too: 'Students must CODA into EE, EE REES, or CPE to take 300 courses.'
engineering.how_you_enter: Two steps: all first-year engineering students are admitted into the Engineering First Year (EFY) program rather than to ECE, then they complete the CODA (Change of Degree Audit) requirements — earliest in December of the first year — to move into Electrical Engineering, EE REES or Computer Engineering. Students in Exploratory Studies or other majors can also take the CODA courses and apply.

door.how_you_enter: Two steps: all first-year engineering students are admitted into the Engineering First Year (EFY) program rather than to ECE, then they complete the CODA (Change of Degree Audit) requirements — earliest in December of the first year — to move into Electrical Engineering, EE REES or Computer Engineering. Students in Exploratory Studies or other majors can also take the CODA courses and apply.
door.easier_than_cs_basis: NC State publishes CODA statistics per major. For 2024-25 overall, Electrical Engineering had 183 first-choice applicants and 176 enrolled, with an EFY middle-50% CODA GPA of 3.22-3.95 and cumulative GPA 3.24-4.01; Computer Engineering had 120 applicants and 112 enrolled with CODA GPA 3.29-3.92; Computer Science had 268 applicants and 259 enrolled with CODA GPA 3.43-3.97. Both EE and CpE therefore show lower matriculant GPA profiles than CS, with CS demand roughly 1.5x EE. Note the caveat: because CODA operates on a guarantee-plus-capacity model rather than a published admit rate, the applicant/enrolled ratios are not admit rates.
door.internal_gate: CODA. The CODA GPA is computed from six Success courses (MA 141, MA 241, PY 205, PY 206, CH 101, CH 102), each of which must be passed with a C or better, and the CODA GPA must be at least 2.0; students must also complete ENG 101, E 101 and E 102 with C- or better and E 115 with an S. Requisites must be completed within four fall/spring semesters. 'Only students in the Engineering First Year program with a CODA GPA greater than or equal 2.0 and a continuation GPA of 2.0 will be guaranteed entrance into at least one of the remaining programs with available seats' — the guarantee is to a program with seats, not to your first choice. Practically, ECE gates course access too: 'Students must CODA into EE, EE REES, or CPE to take 300 courses.'

ece.vs_cs: NC State ECE has the most explicit robotics offering in this batch: a published Controls and Robotics Concentration in the BSEE, 24 hours built on ECE 308 Elements of Control Systems plus a required-elective menu of ECE 441 Robot Motion Planning, ECE 455 Industrial Robotic Systems, ECE 411 Introduction to Machine Learning and ECE 425/525 Neural Networks and Deep Learning, capped by ECE 484/485 Senior Design. As a North Carolina resident the applicant gets in-state consideration at the admission step, but the real gate is CODA after enrollment, and the published statistics show EE matriculants clearing at a lower GPA band (3.22-3.95 CODA GPA) than CS matriculants (3.43-3.97) with far fewer applicants. The cost is a genuine one-year deferral of major identity: you cannot take 300-level ECE courses until you have CODA'd in.
ece.notable: The EE degree also lists an AI & Machine Learning concentration and a Digital Circuits concentration alongside Controls and Robotics. ECE offers an EE/CpE dual degree program reachable through CODA. The earliest an EFY student can CODA is December of the first year, which means a strong fall semester is the whole game.

why_us_ammunition: Co-op is the structural differentiator and is quantifiable: engineering undergraduates typically complete two co-ops on a four-year plan or three on a five-year plan, each usually six months, with terms running January-June or July-December — an applicant can map a concrete AI/robotics co-op sequence [NEU-S4][NEU-S8].

"Almost all students participate in co-op" in the College of Engineering, and every Northeastern undergraduate must complete some form of experiential learning (co-op, research, or service learning) — so an essay can commit to a specific pathway rather than a vague interest [NEU-S4].

The Institute for Experiential Robotics organizes research into five thrusts — human-robot teaming, embodied AI, systems/design/control, ethics-policy-economics, and secure/privacy-preserving robotics — with application areas including manufacturing and extreme environments (space, polar, marine) [NEU-S5][NEU-S9].

IER explicitly recruits undergraduates: its director states "the institute also always provides experiential learning opportunities for our undergraduates. We have a track record of recruiting qualified students in our institute, so they will get involved in our research," with lab space occupying most of the first floor of the EXP research complex [NEU-S6].

Named faculty fits are easy to cite: Taskin Padir (experiential robotics, human-robot teaming at the extremes, embodied AI; RIVeR Lab), Hanumant Singh (SLAM/mapping for aerial, marine and ground vehicles in extreme environments), and Peter Whitney (human-safe, medical and soft robotics) [NEU-S5].
Because Northeastern's CDS shows ED at 43.05% versus 5.21% overall and marks level of interest as Considered, applying ED I is the single largest lever available in this file [NEU-S1].

abet.quote: The BS in Computer Engineering is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, under the commission's General Criteria and Program Criteria for Electrical, Computer, Communications, Telecommunication(s), and Similarly Named Engineering Programs.

robotics_ai.concentration_name: No named robotics concentration inside the BSEE/BSCmpE, but ECE lists Robotics as a curriculum/research area and offers a Minor in Robotics; the combined major route (Computer Engineering and Computer Science) is the school's signature robotics-relevant structure.
robotics_ai.capstone: Two-semester senior design: 'A senior-year design (two-semester) course caps the education', realized as EECE 4791 ECE Capstone 1 and EECE 4792 ECE Capstone 2 in the combined Computer Engineering and Computer Science curriculum.

door.how_you_enter: Direct application to a named major or a combined major: you apply to the College of Engineering for BS Computer Engineering or BS Electrical Engineering, or to an intercollege combined major such as Computer Engineering and Computer Science (College of Engineering plus the Khoury College of Computer Sciences).
door.easier_than_cs_basis: Northeastern does not publish per-major or per-college admit rates on the pages fetched, so no numeric ECE-versus-CS comparison is available. Structurally, the Computer Engineering and Computer Science combined major is an intercollege degree and is 'fully accredited as a Bachelor of Science in Computer Engineering and adds the computer science depth', which means it is admitted through the engineering side rather than as a standalone Khoury CS admit.
door.internal_gate: No published GPA or capacity gate to declare or remain in ECE was found on the pages fetched. The combined-major BSCmpE requires 135 total semester hours.

ece.vs_cs: Northeastern's differentiator is not admissions math but the co-op engine: more than 90 percent of ECE undergraduates do co-op, typically two to three six-month placements, and ECE co-op employers include Amazon Robotics, iRobot, Analog Devices, Apple, Draper, MIT Lincoln Laboratory, Tesla and SpaceX, with the College running a dedicated Robotics Week featuring Amazon Robotics, Boston Dynamics, Shield AI, Symbotic and Piaggio Fast Forward. The combined Computer Engineering and Computer Science major is the strongest single answer to the ECE-versus-CS question here because it is one degree that is ABET-accredited as Computer Engineering while adding CS depth (CS 3000, CS 3650, CS 4530 alongside EECE 2160 Embedded Design: Enabling Robotics and the EECE 4791/4792 capstone). The cost is length and load: 135 semester hours plus co-op cycles push the degree toward five calendar years.
ece.notable: Intercollege combined majors pairing engineering with computer science (Computer Engineering and Computer Science) plus Computer Engineering and Physics, Electrical Engineering and Physics, and Electrical Engineering and Music. ECE offers a Minor in Robotics, an MS in Robotics, and a PlusOne accelerated master's pathway; graduate robotics courses EECE 5550 Mobile Robotics, EECE 5552 Assistive Robotics and EECE 5554 Robotics Sensing and Navigation are ECE-taught and reachable through PlusOne.

name: The Ohio State University
degree_name: BS Electrical and Computer Engineering (direct admit), Control electives + Robotics and Autonomous Systems minor
degree_type: BS in CSE with an AI specialization — no dedicated AI degree exists [OSU-S1] [OSU-S3]

notable_ai_institute: AI(X) Hub (launched autumn 2025, all 15 colleges, six pillars, shared compute commons) plus TDAI (800+ faculty, 50+ disciplines) and 100 new AI faculty hires starting autumn 2026 [OSU-S51] [OSU-S49] [OSU-S53]
notable_undergraduate_research_program: STEP — every second-year student, faculty mentor plus up to $2,000, open regardless of GPA [OSU-S31] [OSU-S32]
fourplusone_available: Yes — open to both CSE and CIS majors
fourplusone_name: Combined BS/MS in Computer Science and Engineering [OSU-S48]
housing_guarantee: Stronger than a guarantee — a two-year on-campus residency requirement for students within two years of high school graduation [OSU-S73] [OSU-S74]
greek_participation: UNK / NOT PUBLISHED — no official percentage accessible; rush cohort grew ~55% since 2021 to nearly 1,900 students, with three new chapters added in 2026 [OSU-S79]
sports_influence: High — Ohio Stadium seats 102,780; 2025 announced home attendance averaged 104,105 (4th nationally), though scanned attendance averaged 88,490 [OSU-S80] [OSU-S81]
recreation_center: RPAC — "more than 600,000 square feet" per official Student Life material (CONFLICTING sources range ~300,000-605,000), five pools, ~$135/semester recreation fee [OSU-S86] [OSU-S87] [OSU-S90] [OSU-S85]
best_fit_reason: A student can build a de facto AI major from 17 free technical-elective hours of 5000-level AI courses, repeat CSE 5539 up to four times, double-count 9 of those credits into an MS, get a funded faculty-mentored sophomore research project regardless of GPA, and do it inside a campus where AI fluency is a graduation expectation.
