score_notes.cs_foundations: BS CSE requires the full spine: CSE 2221/2231 software, 2321/2331 foundations, 2421/2431 systems, and 3341 programming languages, with no systems course omitted [OSU-S7].
score_notes.math_foundations: Requires Math 1151 + 1172, Math 2568 linear algebra, Math 3345, and Stat 3470, but no named optimization course appears in the reviewed requirement sheets [OSU-S7].
score_notes.ai_curriculum_breadth: CSE 3521, 5522, 5523 (ML), 5524 (vision), 5525 (NLP), 5526 (neural networks), 5243 (data mining) and 5442 (HPC deep learning) are all catalogued with undergraduate-reachable prerequisites [OSU-S13i].
score_notes.ai_curriculum_depth: Depth comes from 5000-level electives and CSE 5539, repeatable to 12 credits / 6 completions and taught as fairness-in-ML, advanced NLP and autonomous-driving perception in recent instances [OSU-S17] [OSU-S18] [OSU-S19] [OSU-S20].
score_notes.emerging_ai_topics: The Fall 2024 CSE 5539 section covered transformers, LLMs, parameter-efficient fine-tuning and emergent properties, and the university offers "Unlocking Generative AI" open to all majors [OSU-S18] [OSU-S24].
score_notes.curricular_flexibility: The 126-hour BS CSE leaves 17 hours of open CSE technical electives at 3000+, which is exactly the room needed to stack 5000-level AI courses [OSU-S7] [OSU-S5].
score_notes.course_availability: CSE 3521, 5522 and 5243 require enrollment in the CSE/CIS/ECE/Data Analytics major, and the department states first preference for CSE courses above 2221 goes to majors, with non-majors taking leftover seats [OSU-S15] [OSU-S16] [OSU-S13].
score_notes.undergraduate_research_access: STEP offers every second-year student a faculty mentor plus up to $2,000 regardless of GPA, layered over up to 300 Undergraduate Research Scholar Awards per year with monthly rounds and a $6,000 ten-week library fellowship [OSU-S31] [OSU-S32] [OSU-S34] [OSU-S38].
score_notes.faculty_mentorship: STEP mandates weekly small-group meetings with a faculty mentor through autumn semester, and major status confers an assigned faculty advisor [OSU-S31] [OSU-S12].
score_notes.project_based_learning: The BS CSE requires both a junior project course (CSE 3901/3902/3903) and a capstone (CSE 5911-5915, with 5914 Knowledge-Based Systems recommended for AI), on top of nine-plus OHI/O events per year [OSU-S7] [OSU-S3] [OSU-S44].
score_notes.robotics_autonomy_options: Robotics and Autonomous Systems (RAS); 11 undergrad robotics courses. 14 labs, CAR, 1 competition team.
score_notes.computing_resources: The Ohio Supercomputer Center is "always free for Ohio classroom usage" and offers H100 (96 GB), A100 (80/40 GB) and V100 GPUs, but students need a class code or a faculty PI to be added to a project [OSU-S39] [OSU-S40] [OSU-S41].
score_notes.industry_preparation: Official figures give average starting salaries of $113,161 (CA/WA) and $76,429 (elsewhere), with named employers from Google and Microsoft to Columbus-based Nationwide and Root [OSU-S65].
score_notes.graduate_school_preparation: The combined BS/MS is clean and the BS CSE objectives name graduate study, but no PhD placement, co-authorship or graduate-destination data was published [OSU-S48] [OSU-S4] [OSU-S65].
score_notes.fourplusone_quality: Open to both CSE and CIS majors, 3.5 CPHR and 90 hours at application, up to 9 double-counted credits shortening the combined degree by a full semester, with no GRE mentioned [OSU-S48] [OSU-S63] [OSU-S64].
score_notes.intellectual_energy: OHI/O ran HackOHI/O, MakeOHI/O, ShowOHI/O, Hack AI, BuckeyeCTF, Game I/O and more within the 2025-26 window, and the AI Club met weekly and hosted OpenAI in November 2025 [OSU-S44] [OSU-S57] [OSU-S59].
score_notes.healthy_ambition: Pressure is structural: the CSE/CIS pre-major has been closed to internal switchers since Autumn 2023, closes at capacity, and the major GPA cutoff is reset annually with "not possible to make exceptions" [OSU-S12] [OSU-S13].
score_notes.student_agency: STEP lets a sophomore design and budget their own funded Signature Project across six categories, and 17 free CSE technical-elective hours let a student build a de facto AI major [OSU-S31] [OSU-S32] [OSU-S7].
score_notes.community_within_scale: A two-year on-campus residency requirement plus seventeen theme-based Scholars living-learning programs and a 1,700-student ASC honors community counterbalance a 46,627-undergraduate campus [OSU-S73] [OSU-S45] [OSU-S76] [OSU-S56].
score_notes.technical_club_ecosystem: Active AI Club (weekly, Baker Systems 198, hosted OpenAI Nov 2025), OSU DEV (200+ members, founded 2022), Underwater Robotics (RoboSub 2026), Buckeye AutoDrive (50+ members), plus a Tech Hub directory of a dozen more [OSU-S57] [OSU-S60] [OSU-S61] [OSU-S29] [OSU-S43].
score_notes.nonacademic_club_variety: Ohio State's student-activities office lists more than 1,400 student organizations [OSU-S78].
score_notes.non_greek_social_life: With a rush cohort of roughly 1,900 students against ~46,600 undergraduates, the great majority are unaffiliated — though the official participation percentage is NOT PUBLISHED [OSU-S79] [OSU-S56].
score_notes.campus_engagement: The university's own Student Life Survey found 85.6% of undergraduates involved in at least one of thirteen involvement types [OSU-S77].
score_notes.recreation_facilities: Official Student Life material puts the RPAC at "more than 600,000 square feet" with five pools including an Olympic-size competition pool and 10-meter diving pool, covered by a ~$135 per-semester recreation fee [OSU-S86] [OSU-S87] [OSU-S85].
score_notes.daily_life: A major metro with unlimited free COTA bus access on the Ohio State app and a nonstop Breeze flight to RDU of about 1h 25m [OSU-S93] [OSU-S94] [OSU-S95].

admissions.admit_rate_note: Fall 2025 (Columbus campus): 81,392 applicants, 40,047 admitted, 8,248 enrolled = 49.2% [OSU-S1]. In-state 11,395/25,273 = 45.1%; out-of-state 19,914/42,898 = 46.4%; international 8,738/13,221 = 66.1% [OSU-S1] (INFERRED - division of CDS C1 counts). Note the pattern: OSU's in-state and out-of-state admit rates are nearly identical, but yield differs sharply - 5,609 of 8,248 enrollees are Ohio residents [OSU-S1]. Waitlist: 5,358 offered, 2,278 accepted a place, 2,049 admitted [OSU-S1] - the only school in this batch where the waitlist is a live path.
admissions.major_admit_context: Ohio State admits first-year students as PRE-majors, not majors: 'Students new to OSU are not directly admitted to major status. Instead, they are admitted as pre-majors' [OSU-S8]. To be a pre-CSE student you must be 'directly admitted to the College of Engineering,' where 'Entry into the college is competitive and several factors are considered including ACT/SAT scores, strong college prep curriculum, class rank and GPA'; the alternative CIS option lives in Arts and Sciences with no additional departmental requirements after college admission [OSU-S8]. Both majors a robotics applicant would want are Limited Space Programs reached through the admission-to-major application, and eligibility is restricted by pre-major: 'Computer Science - CSE and CIS pre-majors may apply' and 'Mechanical Engineering - MECH and AERO pre-majors may apply' (Aerospace likewise) [OSU-S6]. By contrast, Chemical, Civil, Electrical and Computer, Environmental, Industrial and Systems, Materials, Welding, Engineering Physics and FABE are 'Space Available Programs' that accept any engineering student in good standing (2.0 GPA or above) without an application [OSU-S6]. The admission-to-major floor is a 2.0 cumulative OSU GPA plus major-specific course criteria (for CS: Calculus I and CSE 2221 with a C or better plus pre-major enrollment, and for the CSE option also Calculus II and Fundamentals of Engineering; for ME: Calculus II, Fundamentals of Engineering, Physics I and enrollment in the aerospace or mechanical pre-major), but admission is capacity-competitive, students rank up to three majors, and 'Admitted students will be offered a place in one major' [OSU-S6]. There are hard limits on second chances - two attempts only, and accepting an offer bars reapplying in the next cycle [OSU-S6]. Front-end choice matters too: applicants wanting Aerospace, Biomedical, CSE, CIS or Mechanical 'must choose one of these programs during their initial application to Ohio State,' admitted students may change into engineering programs only through May 15, and 'After May 15, students will not be permitted to switch into Aerospace Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, Computer Science and Engineering, Computer and Information Science, or Mechanical Engineering programs' [OSU-S7]. Applying Early Action is effectively mandatory for engineering: EA is required for 'Majors in the College of Engineering' as well as merit scholarships and honors [OSU-S3]. No per-major admit rate is published by OSU.
admissions.ed_admit_rate_note: Ohio State offers no Early Decision plan (CDS C21 = No) [OSU-S1].
admissions.ea_admit_rate_note: The 2025-2026 CDS records a non-restrictive EA plan (closing 11/1, notify 1/31) without publishing EA applicant/admit counts [OSU-S1]. The 60.4% EA rate circulating from the 2023-24 CDS was not re-verified in this session.
admissions.test_detail_note: Fall 2025 enrolled: SAT submitted by 25% (2,099), ACT by 42% (3,474) - the only school in this batch where ACT submission exceeds SAT. SAT composite 25th/50th/75th = 1300/1380/1440; ACT 27/30/32 [OSU-S1].
admissions.gpa_note_detail: OSU leaves CDS C11/C12 blank, so no institution-reported GPA distribution or average is available [OSU-S1]. Class rank instead: 73% top tenth, 96% top quarter, 99% top half, with 27% submitting rank [OSU-S1].
admissions.test_policy_2027_cycle: REQUIRED - this is a change from prior cycles and the biggest surprise in this batch. CDS C8 states SAT/ACT are 'Required to be considered for admission' for Fall 2027 [OSU-S1], the admissions site confirms 'Yes, standardized test scores from ACT or SAT are required for first-year applicants to the Columbus campus,' superscoring is used, and the last usable test dates for Early Action are October 3 (SAT) / October 17 (ACT) [OSU-S3]; the university announced the reinstatement publicly [OSU-S5]. CDS C8E gives a latest test date of 1/15 and notes scores are used for advising/placement [OSU-S1].
admissions.c7_note: C7 grid visually confirmed from the CDS page image (the PDF text layer omits the checkbox values). Test scores are Very Important here - the only school in this batch to rate them that highly - consistent with the reinstated requirement. Volunteer work and work experience are both Important, unusually high. Alumni relation and religious affiliation Not Considered; geographical residence and state residency Considered [OSU-S1].

admissions.supplemental_essays_note: Confirms the expectation that OSU has no conventional supplemental essay set for first-year admission [OSU-S4]. Separately, the later admission-to-major application (taken as a current student) does require essays of about 250 words / maximum 1500 characters each, with the major-specific Essay 1 required only for Aerospace, Biomedical, Computer Science (CSE or CIS) and Mechanical Engineering [OSU-S6] - useful to know, but not part of the freshman application.
why_us_ammunition: The Center for Automotive Research is OSU's flagship mobility lab and reports '137 Students Gaining Hands on Research Experience' and '131 Collaborating Faculty' [OSU-S9] - a rare, citable undergraduate-research scale number.

CAR's technical focus - 'Electrification, connectivity, automation, and multi-modal transportation systems' - plus advanced-mobility programming and industry tours in central Ohio gives a specific autonomy/robotics angle [OSU-S10].

OSU's engineering structure is worth addressing head-on: Space Available versus Limited Space programs [OSU-S6] means you can argue why you want a capacity-controlled major (CS or ME) and show you know the 2.0-plus-coursework gate and the three-choice ranking.

The pre-major model means your first-year plan is part of the pitch: Calculus, CSE 2221 or Fundamentals of Engineering, and Physics sequences are the actual admission-to-major currency [OSU-S6] - referencing them signals fit.

Ohio State reinstated the SAT/ACT requirement for first-year applicants [OSU-S3][OSU-S5] and rates test scores Very Important [OSU-S1], so a strong score is itself a why-us-fit argument: this is the one school in the batch where testing carries maximum weight.

robotics_curriculum_detail.score_basis: A real, college-level Robotics and Autonomous Systems (RAS) undergraduate minor with a published 12-credit course list: required ECE/ME 5463 Introduction to Real Time Robotics Systems plus approved electives covering controls (ECE 3551, ME 5372), perception (CSE 5524 Computer Vision, ECE 5200 DSP), planning/autonomy (ECE 5553 Autonomy in Vehicles), industrial robotics (ISE 5520, ISE 5525) and human-centered automation (ISE 5740); undergraduate research credit (4998/4999) counts toward the minor. Rubric 4, not 5: no dedicated robotics degree, and the robotics course stack sits at the 5000 level shared with graduate students rather than forming an 8-course dedicated undergraduate sequence with a robotics capstone. door.how_you_enter: You apply to Ohio State indicating a major; engineering students on the Columbus campus then move into ECE as a 'Space Available Program', which requires only good standing with a 2.0 GPA and no separate major application.
door.easier_than_cs_basis: Published entry-to-major policy differs: ECE is a Space Available Program open to engineering students in good standing with a 2.0 GPA or above 'without the need to submit an admission application', while Computer Science is a Limited Space Program that requires a major application and, per CSE's published mechanism, students 'who have a cumulative GPA of 3.2 or above and have completed the prerequisite courses are admitted to the major' (OSU-E5, OSU-E6). No per-major admit rates are published, so this is a policy-threshold difference rather than a published yield comparison.
door.internal_gate: 2.0 cumulative GPA and good standing in the College of Engineering, no application required (OSU-E5)

ece.vs_cs: Ohio State ECE hands you the physical robot: 73 core credit hours plus 31 hours of ECE electives structured across seven domains, so you can concentrate in Control and still reach across to Computers and Communications/DSP (OSU-E3), with named courses in real-time robotics, feedback control, embedded systems, vehicle autonomy and machine learning for ECE (OSU-E4). CSE gives deeper software, algorithms and AI theory but is enrollment-limited behind a 3.2 GPA gate, whereas ECE admits any engineering student at 2.0 (OSU-E5, OSU-E6). The cost of ECE is a heavier prescribed core with less room for free electives and less software depth.
ece.notable: The Robotics and Autonomous Systems minor requires ECE/ME 5463, so ECE owns the gateway robotics course for the campus-wide minor. Computer engineering BSECE majors take 84 core credit hours plus 20 technical/directed elective hours, a heavier core than the EE program (OSU-E3).

admissions.admit_rate_note: Fall 2025 (West Lafayette): 87,220 applicants, 37,881 admitted, 9,656 enrolled = 43.4% [PU-S1]. In-state 8,559/12,040 = 71.1%; out-of-state 25,650/58,853 = 43.6%; international 3,672/16,327 = 22.5% [PU-S1] (INFERRED - division of CDS C1 counts). Purdue is unusual in this batch: the out-of-state rate (43.6%) is close to the headline rate, so a North Carolina applicant is not structurally penalized at the university level - the selectivity sits inside the major.
admissions.major_admit_context: Purdue admits engineering applicants into First-Year Engineering (FYE), not into a degree program: 'The first year of all Engineering programs at Purdue is common, and incoming students are admitted to First-Year Engineering (FYE) rather than to one of the 16 Engineering degree programs,' and after completing FYE requirements students move through the 'Transition to Major' (T2M) process [PU-S5]. T2M outcomes are good but not guaranteed: 'Over the past five years 93% to 95% of students who have met minimum requirements for transition-to-major have received their first choice,' while 'Admission to Engineering degree programs may be competitive, especially for programs that are at or above enrollment capacity,' judged on GPA, the Engineering Admissions Index (EAI) and other factors [PU-S5]. Two programs are named as capacity-limited: Aeronautical and Astronautical Engineering (AAE) and Mechanical Engineering (ME) - 'Students with a cumulative GPA of 2.99 or below, and who request majors with capacity limitations (currently AAE and ME), will be advised by FYE Advisors' [PU-S5]. So for a robotics applicant targeting ME, first choice is usually granted but a sub-3.0 first year puts it at risk. Computer Science sits outside engineering and is the harder door from inside: CS change-of-degree-objective (CODO) approvals 'will be made on a SPACE AVAILABLE BASIS and will be determined through an academic review of all applicants,' with the highest consideration going to students earning an A- in CS 18000, a B or better in an approved calculus course, and a minimum 3.00 cumulative GPA; students on academic probation are ineligible, only the first or second attempt at a required course counts, and decisions are made at the end of each semester [PU-S6]. Purdue also tells applicants directly that 'Changing majors or locations is never guaranteed' and lets them list a primary major plus an optional alternate [PU-S3]. Practical consequence: name CS on the application if CS is the goal - do not plan to CODO in - and expect ME to be reachable through FYE with a solid first-year GPA.

why_us_ammunition: First-Year Engineering plus Transition to Major is a genuine differentiator to write about: you spend a common first year and then choose among 16 degree programs, with 93-95% of qualified students getting their first choice [PU-S5] - frame it as wanting exposure before committing.

Aeronautics and Astronautics facilities are concrete and quotable: Purdue describes its UAS Research and Test Facility as the 'World's largest Motion Capture facility for UAS research' and claims world leadership in laminar-turbulent transition in hypersonic flows and in Earth remote sensing via reflected satellite transmissions [PU-S8] - strong for drone/autonomy interests.

The Robotics Accelerator exists specifically to pool robotics work across campus - 'Be it for medical, agricultural, search and rescue, assistive robotics, or any other application' - which supports a cross-college robotics narrative [PU-S9].

Purdue publishes a robotics/cyber-physical-systems course landscape spanning AAE, CS and CNIT (e.g. CS 49000 Introduction to Robotics, CNIT 56200 Assistive Technology and Robotics, CNIT 56300 Software Design and Development for Robotics) [PU-S10] - naming courses shows real research.

Purdue counts demonstrated interest (level of applicant's interest = Considered) and weights the essay Very Important [PU-S1], so a specific, Purdue-only 'opportunities' answer in the 250-word question is unusually high-leverage here.

robotics_curriculum_detail.score_basis: Purdue Polytechnic offers a dedicated undergraduate robotics degree — Robotics Engineering Technology, BS — whose catalog plan of study documents a robotics course spine spanning mechanics (MET 11100, MET 21300, MET 31500 Applied Mechanism Kinematics and Dynamics), controls (MFET 24100 Automatic Control Systems, ECET 33700, ECET 30201 Industrial Control Systems for Smart Manufacturing), perception (ECET 36900 Applied Computer Vision for Sensing and Automation), robot kinematics and programming (MFET 34800 Introduction to Robot Kinematics, MFET 24800 Industrial Robot Programming and Applications, MFET 44200 Programming Robots with ROS), autonomy/HRI (MFET 44000 Smart Manufacturing Autonomous Human Robot Systems) and a two-course capstone (MFET 48002 Engineering Technology Capstone I, ENGT 48100 Capstone II). Graduate robotics courses across CS/ECE/ME/IE/AAE add depth. [PUR-R1][PUR-R2][PUR-R3][PUR-R4]

door.how_you_enter: Two steps: you first apply to and are admitted to the College of Engineering (46.1% admit rate), entering First-Year Engineering rather than a named major, and then complete First-Year Engineering requirements and go through the Transition to Major (T2M) process to declare ECE, ranking first and second choices.
door.easier_than_cs_basis: Purdue's published freshman profile gives College of Engineering 46.1% and Computer Science 35.9% (Polytechnic Institute 54.2%), so the admission step into the college that contains ECE is more than 10 points more permissive than the direct Computer Science admit. Purdue's T2M pages further list the capacity-limited majors as Aeronautical & Astronautical Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, Multidisciplinary Engineering and Mechanical Engineering; ECE is not on that list (PURDUE-E3, PURDUE-E4, PURDUE-E5).
door.internal_gate: T2M after First-Year Engineering: complete FYE requirements, then request a major. No published minimum GPA for ECE; FYE advising flags students with cumulative GPA of 2.80 or below only when their first choice is a capacity-limited major (ME, AAE, BME), and ECE is not listed as capacity-limited. The ECE degree itself requires an overall GPA of at least 2.000 in courses applying to the ECE major area.

ece.vs_cs: Purdue ECE gives you a named Automatic Control concentration plus an AI & Machine Learning concentration in either the BSEE or the BSCmpE, so you get feedback control, embedded microprocessor design and robotics coursework (ECE 56900 Introduction to Robotic Systems) inside an EAC-accredited engineering degree. The cost is the First-Year Engineering detour: you cannot declare ECE as an applicant, and you must clear FYE requirements before T2M. Compared with Computer Science, the front door is materially wider (46.1% vs 35.9%) and ECE is not on Purdue's capacity-limited major list, so the second gate is also softer.
ece.notable: ECE lists Quantum Technology and Microelectronics & Semiconductors concentrations alongside AI/ML; ECE prefers CS 15900 as the First-Year Engineering selective, so an ECE-bound student should take the programming selective in FYE. 32 credits of upper-level ECE must be taken at West Lafayette.

score_notes.cs_foundations: Required core spans CSCI 1100, 1200, 2200 Foundations, 2300 Algorithms, 2500 Computer Organization, and 2600 Principles of Software within a 128-credit degree [RPI-S1].
score_notes.math_foundations: The AI/ML/DS Track fixes Math Option I as MATH 2010 and requires CSCI 2210 Mathematical Foundations of Machine Learning, covering matrix decomposition, eigenvalues, vector calculus, continuous probability, and optimization [RPI-S1] [RPI-S3].
score_notes.ai_curriculum_breadth: Dedicated courses exist in ML (4100), RL (4160), CV (4270), ML+optimization (4140), trustworthy ML (4180), decentralized AI (4190), data mining (4390), and graph mining (4280) [RPI-S4]; no dedicated NLP or LLM course was found in CSCI.
score_notes.ai_curriculum_depth: The AI Track requires eight courses totaling ≥30 credits, with 4000-level courses replaceable by co-listed 6000-level graduate versions [RPI-S1].
score_notes.emerging_ai_topics: CSCI 4180 Trustworthy Machine Learning covers alignment and adversarial robustness and CSCI 4170 covers diffusion and generative models [RPI-S4], but no dedicated LLM or AI-agents course was found in the Fall 2026 CSCI catalog listing.
score_notes.curricular_flexibility: 128 credits with a fixed first year (2 CS, 2 math, 2 physics, biology), a 30+-credit Track, HASS core, and a rule that research credits (494x) cannot count toward the Track [RPI-S1].
score_notes.course_availability: SIS publishes explicit frequencies: CSCI 4100 fall annually, CSCI 4150 spring annually, CSCI 4270 fall annually, CSCI 4140 spring annually, CSCI 4480 fall and summer, CSCI 2700 fall/spring/summer annually [RPI-S4] [RPI-S26].
score_notes.undergraduate_research_access: URP pays a minimum $14.20/hr with up to $500/semester subsidized by the Office of Undergraduate Education, and the Summer Undergraduate Research Award pays up to $6,400 for 10 weeks open to all undergraduates [RPI-S18] [RPI-S20].
score_notes.faculty_mentorship: URP is a structured faculty-matching program and the CS co-term requires a prospective MS advisor's letter describing a research project [RPI-S17] [RPI-S49], but AIRC and RAIR present as graduate-centered and no lab page lists undergraduate members.
score_notes.project_based_learning: RCOS has 160+ members and is taken for credit as CSCI 2700 (offered fall/spring/summer annually), and CSCI 4170 is a communication-intensive AI/ML projects course [RPI-S16] [RPI-S26] [RPI-S4].
score_notes.robotics_autonomy_options: BS in Robotics Engineering (joint ECSE + MANE) (EAC); 9 undergrad robotics courses. 5 labs, CATS, 2 competition teams.
score_notes.computing_resources: AiMOS, an 8-petaflop IBM POWER9/NVIDIA V100 system, sits within CCI resources totaling >130,000 cores and ~1,500 GPUs, and an IBM Quantum System One (127-qubit Eagle) has been operational on campus since January 2024 [RPI-S14] [RPI-S15] [RPI-S24].
score_notes.industry_preparation: The CS department reports an average starting salary of $101,923 for the class of 2024 [RPI-S52]; the experiential requirement is a single 260-hour Discovery Semester rather than a multi-term co-op program [RPI-S8].
score_notes.graduate_school_preparation: The CS co-terminal application requires a research-goals statement plus a prospective MS advisor's letter describing a research project or thesis, and undergraduate aid can continue through the 9th-10th semesters [RPI-S49].
score_notes.fourplusone_quality: The Co-Terminal program is established with a published 90-credit and 3.0-GPA threshold and per-program GPA table [RPI-S47] [RPI-S48], but the exact number of double-counted BS/MS credits was not published on any fetched page (UNK).
score_notes.intellectual_energy: RCOS's 160+ members plus a 12th-annual HackRPI (November 15-16, 2025) and a 2026 edition already announced [RPI-S16] [RPI-S40] [RPI-S41].
score_notes.healthy_ambition: Direct major access with no internal AI-track application reduces zero-sum competition [RPI-S1]; grading practices and competitive culture were not documented by any fetched source.
score_notes.student_agency: Undergraduates may substitute co-listed 6000-level courses for Track requirements and may Self-Design the Discovery Semester [RPI-S1] [RPI-S8], but research credits cannot count toward the Track and the 260-hour Discovery requirement is mandatory.
score_notes.community_within_scale: 5,665 full-time undergraduates with both first- and second-year cohorts required to live on campus, plus 200+ clubs [RPI-S36] [RPI-S61] [RPI-S44].
score_notes.technical_club_ecosystem: RCOS (160+ members, credit-bearing, GitHub activity through August 2025) and HackRPI (12th annual in November 2025) are both verifiably active [RPI-S16] [RPI-S38] [RPI-S40].
score_notes.nonacademic_club_variety: The Student Union reports 200+ clubs with a public directory [RPI-S44] [RPI-S45]; participation depth and category breadth were not verified, and the total is modest against 5,665 undergraduates.
score_notes.non_greek_social_life: Greek life involves "more than 1,000 students" across 28 fraternities and 5 sororities (~18% of undergraduates) and carries a documented second-year housing waiver privilege [RPI-S44] [RPI-S61]; 200+ clubs and mandatory two-year residency provide alternatives.
score_notes.campus_engagement: Both first- and second-year cohorts must live on campus with a meal plan, and the Student Union has been "the center of student life since 1890" [RPI-S61] [RPI-S44].
score_notes.recreation_facilities: The Mueller Center's published card-access hours are 7am-11pm Monday-Thursday but only 9am-7pm Saturday [RPI-S65], amenity inventory is unverified, and students report hours limited by staffing [RPI-S66].
score_notes.daily_life: RPI's own Student Senate names "dining hall hours and options" and "campus accessibility" among its key issues, corroborated by recurring student dining complaints [RPI-S54] [RPI-S56]; Troy weather, safety data, and RDU travel were not sourced.

admissions.admit_rate_note: Fall 2025: 14,356 applicants, 9,655 admitted, 1,394 enrolled = 67.3% [RPI-S1]. New York residents 2,917/4,319 = 67.5%; out-of-state 6,125/8,947 = 68.5%; international 613/1,090 = 56.2% [RPI-S1] (INFERRED - division of CDS C1 counts). Residency is irrelevant here, and RPI is by far the least selective school in this batch on paper - the constraint is cost and yield (1,394 enrolled from 9,655 admits), which is why merit and FIRST scholarships matter more than admissibility.
admissions.major_admit_context: RPI admits to a school rather than to a capacity-controlled major: applicants select a program (for example a School of Engineering major or Undeclared Engineering), and the application requires no program-specific essay except for five named programs - Accelerated Physician-Scientist (B.S./M.D.), Architecture, Electronic Arts, Games and Simulation Arts and Sciences, and Music [RPI-S4]. RPI publishes NO major-level or school-level admit rates, and none appear in the CDS [RPI-S1][RPI-S4]; there is likewise no published GPA gate, capacity limit, or restricted change-of-major process for Computer Science or Mechanical Engineering on the pages fetched on 2026-08-16 [RPI-S4]. For a robotics applicant the notable structural feature is curricular rather than competitive: RPI now offers a B.S. in Robotics Engineering 'Jointly administered by the Departments of Electrical, Computer, and Systems Engineering and Mechanical, Aerospace, and Nuclear Engineering,' combining 'mechanical design, electronics, computing, and artificial intelligence' with coursework in sensing, actuation, control and intelligent decision-making [RPI-S5]. Practical consequence: you can apply directly into robotics rather than assembling it from a mechanical or CS degree, and there is no internal admission tournament to survive after arrival - the trade-off is a 67% admit rate that makes RPI a likely-admit whose real question is net price.
admissions.ed_admit_rate_note: CDS 2025-2026: 317 Early Decision applications, 219 admitted = 69.1% (INFERRED - division of CDS C21 counts) [RPI-S1]. The ED rate is essentially identical to the overall rate, so ED at RPI buys certainty and demonstrated commitment (which the CDS marks as Considered), not a statistical edge - and it forfeits the ability to compare aid offers.
admissions.ea_admit_rate_note: CDS C22 records Early Action closing 12/1 with notification 1/29 but publishes no EA applicant/admit counts [RPI-S1].
admissions.test_detail_note: Fall 2025 enrolled: SAT submitted by 53% (733 students), ACT by 13% (180). SAT composite 25th/50th/75th = 1380/1450/1500; ACT 31/33/34 [RPI-S1]. Scores of admitted students are high relative to the admit rate - a strong score is the main merit-aid lever.
admissions.gpa_note: 43% of enrolled first-year students reported a 4.0 GPA; average high school GPA 3.93 with 96% submitting (CDS C11/C12) [RPI-S1]. Class rank: 63% top tenth, 90% top quarter [RPI-S1].
admissions.test_policy_2027_cycle: TEST-OPTIONAL, explicitly for this applicant's cycle: 'Any student who applies to attend Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute as an undergraduate in the fall of 2027 will be able to choose whether or not to submit SAT or ACT scores,' and 'RPI will remain test-optional through the Fall 2030 application cycle' [RPI-S3]. Mechanics: answer the Common App question 'Would you like RPI to consider your ACT/SAT scores as a part of your application file?'; if you say yes, the file is incomplete until scores arrive (official or self-reported); changes require emailing adm_updates@rpi.edu; Regular Decision applicants may use tests taken before January 31; 'not submitting test scores does not lower your chances of admission' and 'RPI does not use test scores to determine student eligibility for merit aid.' Exception: Physician-Scientist (B.S./M.D.) applicants must submit official scores [RPI-S3][RPI-S4].
admissions.c7_note: RPI is one of two schools in this batch that count level of applicant's interest (Considered) [RPI-S1] - campus visits, portal engagement, the optional GLIMPSE video and an ED application all register. Alumni relation Considered; interview, geographical residence, state residency and religious affiliation Not Considered [RPI-S1].

supplemental_essays.prompt: No supplemental essay for engineering, computer science or robotics applicants: 'The general essay/personal statement submitted with your application satisfies RPI's essay requirements, except for applicants to the following programs' (Accelerated Physician-Scientist B.S./M.D., Architecture, Electronic Arts, Games and Simulation Arts and Sciences, Music)

Program-specific prompts, only if applying to those programs - e.g. B.S./M.D.: 'State your reasons for aspiring to a career in medicine.'; Architecture: 'State your reasons for choosing architecture as your profession.'; Electronic Arts, GSAS and Music have their own prompts. Delivered on the Common App writing supplement, which 'must be submitted separately from the Common App itself.'
Optional: 60-90 second GLIMPSE video (U.S. high school students)

admissions.supplemental_essays_note: CONFLICTING with the expectation of two RPI short essays: the official apply page fetched on 2026-08-16 states the general personal statement satisfies the essay requirement for all programs except the five named ones [RPI-S4]. If the live Common App member section adds 'why RPI' questions for 2026-27, treat them as new.
why_us_ammunition: RPI's B.S. in Robotics Engineering is jointly administered by ECSE and MANE and 'provides a rigorous, interdisciplinary education that combines mechanical design, electronics, computing, and artificial intelligence' - a single degree instead of a stitched-together path [RPI-S5].

The program's own rationale cites growing demand and 'increasing K-12 engagement in robotics' - i.e. FIRST-style pipelines are explicitly part of why the degree exists, which makes your FRC record on-thesis rather than incidental [RPI-S5].

Curriculum is explicit about sensing, actuation, control and intelligent decision-making 'within unified robotic systems,' with named strands in Electrical, Computer, Mechanical Engineering and AI/Machine Learning [RPI-S5] - reference specific strands rather than 'robotics' generally.

RPI counts demonstrated interest and alumni relation in review [RPI-S1] and offers the optional GLIMPSE video [RPI-S4], so a visit, a video and (if RPI is a clear first choice) an ED I application are the levers that actually move this file.

The FIRST scholarship pathway is the largest in this batch - up to ten four-year awards with a minimum $12,500/year and $50,000 total - but it is applied for in 11th grade [RPI-S6], so this is the school where FIRST participation can be converted into money earliest.

ece.vs_cs: ECSE is the strongest robotics door at RPI because RPI has no standalone undergraduate robotics degree: robotics arrives as ECSE focus areas ('Robotics and Automation', 'Control Systems', 'Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning', 'Computer Vision and Image Processing'), and completing and declaring one earns a certificate at graduation (RPI-E2). Versus CS you gain circuits, signals, embedded hardware, power and control theory plus the EAC-accredited engineering credential; you give up depth in software systems and theory. RPI's dual-major mechanism makes ECSE+CS realistic - electives can 'Fulfill the course requirements of a dual major,' one diploma is awarded for both majors, and the 24-credit math/science and 24-credit HASS requirements count for both curricula (RPI-E2, RPI-E5).

score_notes.cs_foundations: Intro programming, object-oriented design (CS 2102/2103/2119) and CS 2223 Algorithms are required, but computer systems is not required in the AI major and no theory-of-computation course appears in the tracking sheet [WPI-S4].

score_notes.ai_curriculum_breadth: Named courses span RL (DS/CS 551), generative AI (DS/CS 552), NLP (DS/CS 554), CV (CS/RBE 549), motion planning (RBE 550), HRI (RBE 526) and edge AI (ECE/CS/DS 556), all permitted toward the BS [WPI-S4][WPI-S5].
score_notes.ai_curriculum_depth: AI Core is 8/3 units with at least two of three units required at 4000-level or above, plus a 6/3-unit concentration and a required 9-credit MQP [WPI-S4][WPI-S12].
score_notes.emerging_ai_topics: Dedicated courses exist for Generative Artificial Intelligence (DS/CS 552), Responsible AI (DS 555), ML Development & Operations (DS 553) and On-Device Deep Learning (556) [WPI-S5][WPI-S70].
score_notes.curricular_flexibility: The 15-unit degree carries 6/3 HUA and a 6/3 concentration, leaving few free electives — though eleven concentrations and normal double-majoring provide steerability [WPI-S4][WPI-S1][WPI-S78].
score_notes.course_availability: Catalog eligibility is explicit, but no term class schedule was reachable and the AI major's first tracking sheet is only AY2026-27, so rotation of DS 552/554/551 is unverified [WPI-S4][WPI-S7].
score_notes.undergraduate_research_access: EREE pays $4,500 over 10 weeks and is aimed at first- and second-year students with a faculty-matching committee, and the CUR submission states 100% of full-time faculty involve undergraduates in research [WPI-S26][WPI-S14].
score_notes.faculty_mentorship: The required 9-credit MQP gives every senior a faculty-advised research project, and A&S research pages name individual undergraduate fellows with their advisors (e.g., a CS+RBE double major with Prof. Whitehill) [WPI-S12][WPI-S27].
score_notes.project_based_learning: Two required 9-credit projects (IQP junior year, MQP senior year), 70% of courses include project activities, 90% complete an off-campus project, 918 off-campus IQPs in 2019-20 [WPI-S11][WPI-S14][WPI-S12].
score_notes.robotics_autonomy_options: BS in Robotics Engineering (EAC); 13 undergrad robotics courses. 15 labs, Robotics Engineering Department, 4 competition teams.
score_notes.computing_resources: No public GPU inventory or undergraduate cluster-access policy was found; PracticePoint provides physical labs rather than compute [WPI-S73][WPI-S74].
score_notes.industry_preparation: Corporate-sponsored MQPs with sponsors including MITRE, Pfizer, Barclays, DraftKings and BNP Paribas, plus PracticePoint members GE Healthcare and Boston Scientific [WPI-S25][WPI-S73].
score_notes.graduate_school_preparation: Required faculty-advised MQP plus open graduate AI courses are strong ingredients, but no published grad-school destination list or undergraduate publication record was found [WPI-S12][WPI-S44].
score_notes.fourplusone_quality: BS/MS in AI exists with up to 12 credits or 40% of the MS double-counted at grade B or higher and a 20% alumni tuition incentive [WPI-S6][WPI-S38].
score_notes.intellectual_energy: Students across five independent threads describe 35–45 hour academic weeks in a collaborative atmosphere, with 91% first-to-second-year retention [WPI-S63][WPI-S59][WPI-S11].
score_notes.healthy_ambition: The registrar awards only A, B, C or NR, and NR does not appear on transcripts or grade reports — removing the mechanical basis for grade competition [WPI-S15][WPI-S11].
score_notes.student_agency: Eleven AI concentrations including "Design Your Own"-style breadth options, HECCMA cross-registration, and student-initiated events like the club-run PLAnt competition with 26 robots [WPI-S1][WPI-S67][WPI-S47].
score_notes.community_within_scale: 93% of first-years live on campus, first- and second-year residency is now required for the Class of 2030, and IQP project centers place 24–28 students abroad with two resident faculty [WPI-S21][WPI-S51][WPI-S12].
score_notes.technical_club_ecosystem: 15 robotics/technology clubs demonstrated at the 2025-09-09 Robotics Clubs Showcase, and the Robotics Club ran its own 26-robot combat event on 2025-09-26 [WPI-S46][WPI-S47].
score_notes.nonacademic_club_variety: No student-organization directory was retrieved in this session; only technical clubs were verified [WPI-S46][WPI-S47].
score_notes.non_greek_social_life: Greek participation is high for a tech school (26% of men, 25% of women per CDS) and students report thin Worcester nightlife outside Greek/house parties, though a strong LGBTQ community is also described [WPI-S21][WPI-S59][WPI-S60].
score_notes.campus_engagement: Required first- and second-year residency plus Innovation Studio hours to midnight weeknights and 1 a.m. weekends indicate an evening-active campus [WPI-S51][WPI-S31].
score_notes.recreation_facilities: Sports & Recreation Center opens at 6 a.m. weekdays and closes at 11 p.m. daily, with a pool and posted membership terms [WPI-S33][WPI-S34].
score_notes.daily_life: Campus is 1.5 miles from Union Station with MBTA commuter rail to Boston (~$11.50 each way per students) and free SNAP evening shuttles, but Boston is an hour away and Worcester nightlife is reported as limited [WPI-S55][WPI-S57][WPI-S60].

admissions.overall_admit_rate_note: Fall 2025: 12,355 applied / 7,647 admitted / 1,300 enrolled (CDS C1). Fall 2024 was 60.2% (12,559 / 7,555).
admissions.admit_rate_note_note: WPI's CDS does not publish an in-state vs out-of-state admit split.
admissions.major_admit_context: WPI admits to the university, not to a capped major: applicants indicate an intended major on the Common Application and there is no separate, more selective admission gate for Robotics Engineering. The practical 'direct-admit' benefit is financial rather than academic — WPI states that students who indicate Robotics Engineering as their intended major are automatically considered for Robotics Engineering Scholars awards of typically $10,000-$25,000 per year renewable for four years [WPI-S9]. WPI's Robotics Engineering department describes its BS program as 'first-of-its-kind in the nation and the most comprehensive in the world' [WPI-S10]. Selectivity is instead concentrated in the application plan: Early Decision I admitted 310 of 397 applicants (78.1%) for Fall 2025 versus 69.3% Early Action and 61.9% overall, and ED admits receive a minimum $25,000 scholarship plus a free summer course [WPI-S1][WPI-S3].
admissions.ed_admit_rate_note: Fall 2025 ED: 397 applications, 310 admits (CDS C21). Fall 2024: 279 apps / 211 admits.
admissions.ea_admit_rate_note: Fall 2025 EA: 8,882 applications, 6,151 admits, 858 enrolled (CDS C22). EA is non-restrictive.
admissions.sat_mid50_note: WPI leaves CDS section C9 blank/'not reported' in both 2024-25 and 2025-26 — no score percentiles are published, consistent with its 2021-2024 test-blind period.
admissions.gpa_note: CDS C12 average high school GPA 3.9, reported for 88% of enrolled first-years; CDS C10 shows 51% in the top tenth of their class. WPI's admissions site states an average GPA of 3.92 and average class rank in the top 9%.
admissions.test_policy_note: CDS C8 marks SAT/ACT 'Not Required for Admission, but Consider if Submitted (Test-Optional)' explicitly for the Fall 2027 cycle. WPI was test-blind 2021-2024 and returned to test-optional beginning with the Class of 2030 (Fall 2026 entry) per a November 2024 faculty Committee on Academic Policy motion; WPI describes it as a 'no-harm' practice and asks on the Common Application whether scores should be considered.

interview.mechanism: No evaluative admissions interview; CDS C7 marks Interview 'Not Considered'. WPI will, however, 'consider Initialview or Vericant interviews if submitted' from international applicants as a supplement to English-proficiency evidence.

robotics_ai.capstone: Major Qualifying Project (MQP): a 'team-based, professional-level design or research experience' that is 'the culmination of WPI's project-based undergraduate education' and a requirement of every graduating senior; ECE MQP examples on the BS ECE page include traffic-light detection for self-driving cars, radio communications for a robotic aerial vehicle, a robotic sailboat and a semi-autonomous wheelchair (WPI-E7, WPI-E2).

door.how_you_enter: You apply to WPI itself through the Common Application (single first-year application with ED/EA/RD timing options) and are not admitted to ECE as a separate unit; WPI's Robotics Engineering page tells applicants 'Undecided? No problem. Apply now and explore before committing to a specific path.'
door.easier_than_cs_basis: WPI's first-year application pages describe one university-wide Common Application process with no major-specific admission criteria and publish no per-major admit rates (WPI-E8, WPI-E10).

ece.vs_cs: WPI already has an EAC-accredited Robotics Engineering degree, so ECE is not the robotics door here — it is the hardware-depth door: circuits, microelectronics, embedded computing, signals, control systems and power that neither CS nor the interdisciplinary RBE core covers to the same depth (WPI-E5, WPI-E4). What ECE costs you relative to RBE is the integrated robotics core itself (manipulation, mechanics, robot software stack), and relative to CS you trade algorithms/software breadth for circuit and signal depth. WPI's structure makes doubling up cheap in principle: the Robotics Engineering page lists Electrical & Computer Engineering among potential minors, and ECE offers a minor with clusters in control and power, signals, analog and RF (WPI-E6, WPI-E2) — but WPI does not publish how many students actually pair RBE with an ECE major, so treat 'commonly double up' as unverified.
ece.notable: ECE offers a BS/MS in five years and an ECE minor with clusters in control and power, signals, analog and RF (WPI-E2); the ECE department in Atwater Kent Laboratories lists research in machine learning, signal processing, autonomous vehicles, prosthetic control and microelectronics (WPI-E1); WPI's engineering accreditation page confirms both 'electrical and computer engineering' and 'robotics engineering' programs are EAC-accredited (WPI-E4).

cost_note: VERIFIED with a caveat on scope. WPI's direct-billed 2025-26 total is $83,146 (tuition and fees $63,046 + room and board $18,900 + books $1,200).
